records.title: Battery swelling and heat isolation card
records.summary: Stop charging, avoid pressure or puncture, move people away, and place the device only where this can be done without handling a smoking or burning battery.
records.content: Call emergency services for fire, smoke, rapid heating, hissing, or inability to isolate the area safely. Do not put a damaged lithium battery in a pocket, normal rubbish, or an enclosed container.

records.title: Burn first-actions and escalation card
records.summary: Stop the burning source when safe, cool the burn with cool running water, remove nearby jewellery or loose clothing not stuck to skin, and protect with a clean non-fluffy cover.
records.content: Call emergency help for large, deep, electrical, chemical, airway, face, hand, genital, major-joint burns or any severe symptoms. Do not apply ice, butter, toothpaste, oils, powders, or break blisters.

records.title: Chemical splash eye-exposure first response
records.summary: Move away from the source, begin immediate gentle rinsing with clean water when safe, remove contact lenses if they come out easily, and call emergency or poison guidance.
records.content: Bring the product label or a photo without delaying rinsing or exposing another person. Do not neutralize the chemical with another chemical or rub the eye.

records.title: Coastal storm-surge retreat line
records.summary: Identify higher ground reachable without crossing beaches, river mouths, underpasses, sea walls, or roads already taking waves.
records.content: Leave on official warning or clear rapid water rise rather than watching from the shore. Do not approach the sea, harbour, cliffs, or flooded roads for photographs.

records.title: Power-outage refrigerator decision clock
records.summary: Write the time power failed, keep doors closed, group verified cold items, and prepare a discard decision using official food-safety guidance.
records.content: When temperature or outage history is uncertain, choose the safer discard option for perishable food. Never taste food to test whether it stayed safe.
warnings: Never taste food to test whether it stayed safe.

records.title: Cold-stress buddy observation card
records.summary: Check shivering, speech, coordination, alertness, wet clothing, wind exposure, and the ability to warm safely.
records.content: Move to shelter, remove wet layers when safe, insulate, and call emergency help for confusion, reduced consciousness, or severe deterioration. Do not use direct intense heat on numb skin or give alcohol as a warming method.

records.title: Conflict de-escalation pause protocol
records.summary: Separate immediate safety from the disputed issue, lower voices, reduce the audience, identify needs, and appoint a neutral timekeeper.
records.content: Pause the decision when fatigue, weapons, intoxication, threats, or loss of control are present and move to safety. Do not surround, shame, touch, corner, or threaten a distressed person.

records.title: Offline backup restore rehearsal
records.summary: Test that contacts, identity copies, maps, medical list, manuals, and project data can be opened on a second device without internet.
records.content: Keep at least one protected copy disconnected from the main device. Do not assume a file exists because its name appears in a cloud or recent-files list.

records.title: Earthquake aftershock sleeping-zone check
records.summary: Move sleeping places away from glass, tall furniture, damaged walls, hanging objects, gas smells, and blocked exits.
records.content: Use an outdoor or officially approved shelter when the building shows serious damage or authorities restrict entry. Do not re-enter a damaged building to retrieve nonessential property.

records.title: Greece 112 emergency call message card
records.summary: Prepare a concise message with exact location, what happened, number of people, immediate dangers, and a callback number.
records.content: Call 112 free of charge when immediate police, fire, ambulance, coast guard, or coordinated emergency help is needed. Do not end the call until the operator says to do so unless remaining connected creates danger.

records.title: Critical-device charging priority table
records.summary: Rank medical devices, emergency communication, lights, navigation, refrigeration monitoring, and comfort devices by life-safety effect and remaining runtime.
records.content: Assign charging windows and stop low-priority use before the reserve reaches the emergency floor. Do not connect an unknown device or damaged cable to the last trusted power source.

records.title: Household reunion plan after separation
records.summary: Choose one nearby and one out-of-area meeting point, an out-of-area contact, pickup rules, child safeguards, and written copies for each person.
records.content: Use the safest official route and update the contact rather than repeatedly changing meeting points. Do not publish private household locations or child information on public channels.

records.title: Emergency cash and document packet
records.summary: Keep small cash denominations, identity copies, insurance and property references, emergency contacts, medication list, and essential account recovery details protected.
records.content: Store encrypted or sealed backups in more than one safe location when lawful and practical. Do not keep every original document, password, and all cash in the same bag.

records.title: Food exposed to floodwater discard boundary
records.summary: Separate anything touched by floodwater, sewage, chemicals, damaged packaging, rust, swelling, leakage, or broken seals.
records.content: Discard unsafe items according to official food-safety guidance and document losses for aid or insurance. Do not wash and reuse food in cardboard, cloth, screw-top, snap-lid, or damaged containers after flood exposure.

records.title: Floodwater home re-entry boundary
records.summary: Check official clearance, structural movement, electricity, gas, sewage, chemicals, animals, mould, and safe access before entry.
records.content: Delay entry when power, structure, contamination, or ventilation cannot be made safe. Do not allow children, pets, or unprotected people into contaminated flood areas.

records.title: Generator carbon-monoxide boundary
records.summary: Place any fuel-burning generator outdoors, far from doors, windows, vents, and occupied spaces, following the manufacturer and local fire guidance.
records.content: Shut it down and move people to fresh air when carbon-monoxide alarm, headache, dizziness, nausea, confusion, or unusual sleepiness occurs. Never operate a generator in a home, garage, balcony enclosure, basement, shed, or near an opening.

records.title: Emergency handwashing station flow
records.summary: Arrange clean water or approved hand-cleaning product, soap, controlled dispensing, drainage, drying, and a clear dirty-to-clean direction.
records.content: Place it before food handling, after toilet use, after waste or animal care, and near sick-person care. Do not let wastewater pool near living areas or drinking-water storage.

records.title: Heatwave night-room cooling plan
records.summary: Track indoor temperature, open safely when outdoor air is cooler, block daytime sun, reduce indoor heat sources, and identify a cooler fallback place.
records.content: Move vulnerable people to a cooler place before symptoms become severe. Do not sacrifice fire safety, security, or smoke protection to create airflow.

records.title: Heatwave cool-hours work schedule
records.summary: Move heavy tasks to the coolest practical hours, add water and shade breaks, use a buddy check, and reduce workload for vulnerable people.
records.content: Stop activity and seek urgent help for confusion, fainting, seizures, collapse, or severe worsening. Do not push through symptoms to finish a shift or journey.
warnings: Do not push through symptoms to finish a shift or journey.

records.title: Emergency plan one-page household summary
records.summary: Fit contacts, meeting points, evacuation triggers, medical needs, pets, utility shutoff boundaries, document location, and three priority actions on one page.
records.content: Give every member a paper copy and rehearse how it changes for fire, earthquake, flood, heat, and outage. Do not bury the first actions inside a long manual that no one can open under stress.

records.title: Infant-feeding emergency protection plan
records.summary: Keep the infant with the caregiver, protect breastfeeding support where applicable, secure safe water and clean feeding equipment, and contact health professionals early.
records.content: Use ready-to-feed products when officially advised and available if safe water or cleaning cannot be assured. Do not dilute formula, make homemade formula, or change feeding without qualified guidance.

records.title: Rumour verification board during crisis
records.summary: Create columns for claim, source, time, independent confirmation, official status, action taken, and expiry.
records.content: Act immediately only on direct danger or verified official instruction; otherwise label uncertainty and keep checking. Do not forward frightening claims merely because several people repeat the same original source.

records.title: Tool and spare-part compatibility ledger
records.summary: Record tool size, fastener type, battery platform, voltage, connector, belt, filter, seal, lubricant, manual, and compatible substitutes.
records.content: Test compatibility on noncritical equipment before an emergency repair. Do not force a near-fitting electrical, pressure, fuel, or structural part into service.

records.title: Livestock heat and water triage
records.summary: Check water flow, shade, crowding, breathing, standing ability, feed access, and the most vulnerable animals first.
records.content: Contact a veterinarian or agricultural authority early when multiple animals are affected or water quality is uncertain. Do not force transport during peak heat without a safer destination and ventilation plan.

records.title: Low-bandwidth family status message
records.summary: Use one short format: name, safe or needs help, location, people together, urgent need, battery level, and next check-in time.
records.content: Send text before voice or media when networks are congested and confirm receipt. Do not repeatedly resend large photos or videos unless responders request them.

records.title: Offline map hazard annotation standard
records.summary: Use date, source, direction, status, confidence, and expiry time for every blocked road, water point, shelter, clinic, fire, flood, or landslide mark.
records.content: Cross out obsolete information without erasing the history needed for review. Do not mark an unverified rumour as a confirmed route closure or safe point.

records.title: Medication continuity grab sheet
records.summary: List medicine name, strength, schedule, reason, prescriber, pharmacy, allergies, storage needs, remaining supply, and a photo of the original label.
records.content: Contact a pharmacist or clinician before substitution, dose change, sharing, crushing, splitting, or stopping a prescription. Do not rely on memory alone for high-risk or time-critical medicines.

records.title: Menstrual-hygiene continuity kit
records.summary: Store preferred products, clean underwear, opaque disposal bags, hand-cleaning supplies, pain-relief information, and a private washing plan.
records.content: Increase privacy, water, and disposal access rather than forcing one product on everyone. Seek medical help for very heavy bleeding, fainting, severe pain, pregnancy concern, fever, or sudden major change.

records.title: Mould cleanup stop conditions
records.summary: Identify water source, affected area, porous materials, ventilation, protective equipment, and vulnerable occupants before cleaning.
records.content: Use professional or official guidance for large areas, sewage, hidden growth, HVAC contamination, repeated return, or severe symptoms. Do not dry-brush, sand, or spread contaminated dust through occupied rooms.

records.title: Neighbourhood vulnerability and resource map
records.summary: With consent, mark people who may need checks, accessible routes, water points, first-aid skills, tools, pets, generators, hazards, and communication gaps.
records.content: Keep the detailed map private and share only the information needed for a task. Do not label people publicly by diagnosis, disability, immigration status, wealth, or vulnerability.

records.title: Pet evacuation carrier readiness
records.summary: Keep a carrier or secure lead, identification, recent photo, food, water, medicines, waste supplies, vaccination information, and a familiar cloth ready.
records.content: Practise calm entry into the carrier and identify shelters or contacts that accept animals. Do not release a frightened animal in an unfamiliar evacuation area.
warnings: Do not release a frightened animal in an unfamiliar evacuation area.

records.title: Greece poison centre information card
records.summary: Keep the product container, label, exposure time, route, amount if known, age, symptoms, and medicines ready for the call.
records.content: Contact 112 for severe symptoms and the Greek Poison Centre at 210 7793777 for specialist poisoning information. Do not induce vomiting or give a home remedy unless a qualified professional instructs it.

records.title: 72-hour kit reality audit
records.summary: Carry the kit through the actual exit route, test weight, open every container, check dates, confirm medicines and documents, and simulate one meal and one night.
records.content: Adjust the kit to the weakest person, local heat, walking distance, transport, pets, and likely hazards. Do not count an item as available until someone can find and use it in darkness or stress.

records.title: Grief and acute-stress support boundary
records.summary: Offer safety, calm presence, practical help, water, privacy, contact with trusted people, and clear information without forcing discussion.
records.content: Seek urgent professional help when there is immediate danger, inability to care for basic needs, severe confusion, violence, or risk of self-harm. Do not promise outcomes, demand a detailed retelling, or use alcohol or unprescribed medicine as emotional first aid.

records.title: Radio emergency message format
records.summary: Send call sign or identity, exact location, time, situation, assistance needed, hazards, people affected, and when you will listen again.
records.content: Repeat critical numbers and locations and ask the receiver to read them back. Do not transmit private medical details or names on an open channel unless necessary for care.

records.title: Dry-staple ration and nutrition board
records.summary: Count people, age and health needs, cooking fuel, water, allergens, expiry, and calories only as one part of a balanced plan.
records.content: Set a review date and protect extra portions for illness, pregnancy, heavy work, and delayed resupply. Do not create a starvation ration while edible stock is being lost to poor inventory or spoilage.

records.title: Emergency supply issue and return ledger
records.summary: Record item, quantity, condition, recipient, purpose, issue time, expected return or consumption, and final status.
records.content: Use transparent priorities for scarce items and publish the rule without exposing private medical details. Do not let undocumented borrowing empty the last reserve.

records.title: Rural road isolation resupply trigger
records.summary: Track road condition, weather, fuel, water, medicines, animal feed, communication, and the number of days before each critical supply fails.
records.content: Request help while communication and a safe route still exist, not after the last supply is gone. Do not send one unprepared person alone onto an unverified road.
warnings: Do not send one unprepared person alone onto an unverified road.

records.title: Missing-person last-known-point record
records.summary: Record full description, clothing, photo, medical or mobility needs, exact last-known place and time, planned route, contacts, and who verified each fact.
records.content: Contact emergency authorities promptly and preserve messages, tracks, and belongings that may help trained search teams. Do not send untrained people into dangerous terrain or contaminate the last-known area.

records.title: Seed viability small-batch test
records.summary: Test a labelled small sample under appropriate moisture and temperature before committing scarce soil, water, and labour.
records.content: Record germination count, time, mould, abnormal seedlings, seed age, and storage history. Do not mix unverified seed lots or save visibly diseased seed for critical planting.

records.title: Severe-weather shelter decision log
records.summary: Record warning source, expected timing, wind or water direction, safest room, evacuation route, vulnerable people, animals, and the next decision time.
records.content: Move before roads, stairs, bridges, or visibility become unsafe. Do not travel merely because the current location is uncomfortable when the route is more dangerous.

records.title: Sewer-backup clean-dirty boundary
records.summary: Block access, protect drinking water and food, stop spread through footwear and tools, ventilate safely, and arrange qualified cleanup.
records.content: Relocate vulnerable people when sewage affects living, food, or sleeping areas. Do not use household bleach mixtures or improvised chemical combinations without official product instructions.

records.title: Mutual-aid shift handover sheet
records.summary: Record people present, urgent risks, completed tasks, open tasks, supplies, equipment faults, vulnerable-person checks, and next decisions.
records.content: Read the handover aloud and require the incoming lead to repeat the top three priorities. Do not let a tired person leave before critical hazards and missing people are acknowledged.

records.title: Wildfire smoke clean-room setup
records.summary: Choose the room with the fewest exterior openings, close avoidable air leaks, keep indoor air clean, and monitor official evacuation guidance.
records.content: Use the room only while the building remains safe and authorities do not instruct evacuation. Do not use a smoke room as a reason to remain in the path of an approaching fire.

records.title: Temporary repair expiry label
records.summary: Write the defect, temporary method, load limit, forbidden uses, installer, date, inspection interval, and replacement deadline directly beside the repair.
records.content: Remove the item from service when the limit cannot be enforced. Do not hide a temporary repair under paint, tape, furniture, or a new cover.
steps: Remove the item from service when the limit cannot be enforced.

records.title: Portable toilet service schedule
records.summary: Assign location, privacy, hand cleaning, liner or container control, user limits, service time, waste route, and closure conditions.
records.content: Increase service frequency before overflow, odour, insects, leakage, or hand-cleaning failure appears. Do not place waste storage uphill or upstream from drinking water, food, or sleeping areas.

records.title: Volunteer task competency boundary
records.summary: Match each task to training, physical ability, protective equipment, supervision, legal limits, and the right to refuse.
records.content: Use untrained volunteers for low-risk support while specialists handle medical, electrical, gas, structural, chemical, and rescue work. Do not reward risky improvisation or punish someone for reporting a hazard.

records.title: Household drinking-water reserve rotation
records.summary: Store labelled containers in a cool protected place, record fill or purchase date, inspect for damage, and rotate before trust is lost.
records.content: Keep additional water for hot climates, pregnancy, illness, disability, pets, and longer outages where practical. Do not refill a contaminated or chemical container for drinking water.

records.title: Water-treatment decision hierarchy
records.summary: Prefer sealed commercial water, then officially verified supplies, then an official household-treatment method suitable for the known hazard.
records.content: When chemical, radiological, fuel, salt, or industrial contamination is suspected, seek a different source and official advice. Do not assume boiling removes chemicals, salt, fuel, or radioactive material.

records.title: Wildfire pre-evacuation trigger board
records.summary: List official alert level, wind direction, smoke visibility, road status, vulnerable people, animals, vehicle availability, and the latest safe departure time.
records.content: Leave early when authorities instruct evacuation or when the planned route may soon become unsafe. Do not wait for flames to become visible before acting on verified evacuation instructions.

records.title: Low-water laundry priority
records.summary: How to decide what must be washed first when water, soap, or drying space is limited.
records.content: Not all laundry has equal priority. Under shortage, prioritize underwear, socks, cloths used for wounds or infants, items contaminated by waste, and clothes causing skin problems. Separate sickroom laundry if possible. Dry fully before storage to avoid mold and odor.
steps: Sort by health priority, not appearance.
Wash small critical batches.
Keep dirty and clean areas separate.
Dry items completely.
Record soap and water use if supply is tight.
warnings: Do not store damp fabric in closed bags.
Do not mix wound cloths with kitchen cloths.

records.title: Fair distribution ledger
records.summary: A simple ledger for shared supplies that reduces arguments and hidden depletion.
records.content: Shared supplies disappear when distribution is not visible. A ledger records item, quantity, date, receiver group, reason, remaining stock, and next review. It should not humiliate people. Use categories instead of private details when possible. Fairness includes special needs, not equal portions for unequal risk.
steps: Record every distribution immediately.
Track remaining stock after each change.
Separate privacy-sensitive needs.
Review shortages at fixed times.
Explain rule changes clearly.
warnings: Do not use the ledger to punish people.
Do not hide shortages until supplies are gone.

records.title: Learning rotation for rebuilding skills
records.summary: A low-pressure way for groups to teach basic useful skills without depending on one expert.
records.content: Knowledge becomes fragile when only one person can do a task. Create short teaching rotations: water records, food ledger, tool safety, first aid basics, seed notes, cooking safety, and radio/phone discipline. Teach one safe skill at a time and record who can now help.
steps: Pick one skill per session.
Demonstrate slowly.
Let a learner repeat the safe parts.
Write the checklist.
Assign a backup person for each critical task.
warnings: Do not teach dangerous repairs as casual lessons.
Do not shame slow learners.
common_mistakes: Working from memory only for Learning rotation for rebuilding skills.

records.title: Low-tech inventory tags
records.summary: A tag system for boxes, shelves, tools, food, water, medicine, and repair parts.
records.content: When supplies are scattered, people waste time and duplicate work. Use large tags: category, count, date checked, owner/contact if needed, and use priority. Red tags can mean do not use without permission, yellow can mean check first, green can mean ready. Choose any colors or symbols that the group understands.
steps: Tag every storage box.
Write count and last check date.
Mark restricted or fragile items clearly.
Update tags after every use.
Keep the tag system simple.
warnings: Do not hide dangerous items behind vague labels.
Do not make codes so complex nobody uses them.

records.title: Local recovery priorities meeting
records.summary: A calm meeting format for deciding what to repair, clean, share, or ask for first.
records.content: Recovery can become chaotic if every person pushes a different urgent task. A priorities meeting uses one list: life and health, water, sanitation, shelter, food, communication, access, records, and comfort. Keep meetings short, factual, and recorded. Good recovery meetings protect attention. Start with confirmed facts, then list blockers, then assign only a few tasks that can be finished before the next review. Do not let the loudest person define every priority. Keep unresolved items visible instead of arguing them repeatedly.
steps: Start with confirmed facts.
Rank tasks by safety impact.
Assign names and review times.
Write what cannot be solved locally.
End with the next meeting time.
warnings: Do not let the loudest person become the only priority.
Do not ignore sanitation because repairs feel more visible.
common_mistakes: Working from memory only for Local recovery priorities meeting.

records.title: Community repair day plan
records.summary: A structured repair day that groups tools, skills, safety checks, and priority jobs.
records.content: Repair days can restore many small things if they are organized. First choose safe jobs, gather tools, assign skilled helpers, and separate unsafe repairs. Make a waiting list. Label temporary repairs. Stop before darkness or exhaustion causes injury. A repair day also needs a stop rule, a tool return point, a parts table, drinking water, and a person who refuses unsafe jobs. Small successful repairs build confidence, but unclear repairs create hidden danger. Record every temporary patch, who checked it, and when it must be reviewed again.
steps: Collect repair requests.
Rank by safety and usefulness.
Match tasks to skill level.
Create a parts table.
Mark temporary repairs clearly.
warnings: Do not attempt electrical, gas, structural, or pressure repairs beyond competence.
Do not work tired with sharp tools.
common_mistakes: Working from memory only for Community repair day plan.

records.title: Seed storage dry box
records.summary: A simple way to keep seeds dry, labeled, protected, and useful for later planting.
records.content: Seeds lose value when they are mixed, damp, overheated, eaten by pests, or saved without names. A dry seed box turns seed saving into a usable system. Every packet needs crop name, variety if known, source, year, location, and notes about how the plant performed. Keep food seeds away from chemicals, fuel, and wet tools.
steps: Dry seeds fully before storage.
Label each packet before mixing anything.
Store in a cool, dry, dark place.
Check monthly for moisture, insects, and mold.
Plant older seed in test rows before depending on it.
warnings: Do not save moldy seed.
Do not store seed beside cleaners, fuels, or pesticides.

records.title: Temporary sleeping area layout
records.summary: A layout for sleep, privacy, airflow, trip safety, noise, and vulnerable people in crowded conditions.
records.content: Crowded sleep areas fail when paths, waste, wet clothes, children, pets, and supplies overlap. Keep a clear walking path, one quiet zone, one family zone, one care zone, and one storage edge. Keep lights reachable and exits visible. A sleeping area is also a fire, hygiene, privacy, and caregiving plan. Put people who need frequent help near access routes, keep wet items away from bedding, and make a small night path to water and toilet needs. Review the layout after the first night because real movement shows problems plans miss.
steps: Mark walking paths.
Place vulnerable people near helpers but not in traffic.
Keep wet items outside sleeping zones.
Keep exits visible.
Set quiet hours.
warnings: Do not block exits.
Do not place candles in sleeping areas.

records.title: Mold prevention after dampness
records.summary: A first-response plan for drying rooms, fabrics, papers, and stored supplies after damp conditions.
records.content: Dampness can ruin bedding, papers, food packaging, and indoor air. First stop the water source if safe, separate wet items, increase safe airflow, and dry critical items. Do not seal damp materials in plastic for long storage. Watch for musty smell and visible growth. People with breathing problems may need to avoid affected rooms.
steps: Stop or divert water if safe.
Move dry supplies away from damp zones.
Separate wet fabrics and papers.
Ventilate when outdoor air is safe.
Check daily until fully dry.
warnings: Do not ignore mold smell.
Do not dry contaminated flood items in living spaces without caution.

records.title: Compost safety boundaries
records.summary: A cautious compost system that avoids attracting pests or contaminating food areas.
records.content: Compost can improve soil, but bad compost can attract pests, smell, and spread contamination. Keep compost away from drinking water, food preparation, sleeping areas, and children’s play spaces. Avoid meat, diapers, sickroom waste, chemicals, and unknown materials. Keep a record of what goes in.
steps: Choose a site away from water and food areas.
Add plant scraps and dry carbon material when available.
Cover fresh food scraps.
Keep tools separate from kitchen tools.
Use finished compost cautiously and avoid direct contact with ready-to-eat plant parts.
warnings: Do not compost human waste in a normal household compost pile.
Do not compost chemical-contaminated material.

records.title: Roof and balcony object control
records.summary: A safety check for loose objects before wind, storm, or long absence.
records.content: Loose objects become hazards in wind and can also block drains. Before weather worsens, move or secure pots, chairs, tools, boards, antennas, buckets, and trash. Check drains without leaning over unsafe edges. Do not climb during active bad weather. Treat every object above head height as a possible injury source. Work from safe standing positions only, keep children away from the drop zone, and avoid last-minute fixes in high wind or rain. Record what was moved, what stayed, and what still needs a proper mount or removal.
steps: Walk the area before weather arrives.
Move loose items indoors or low and secure.
Clear safe drains if reachable.
Keep balcony exit usable.
Record damage after weather passes.
warnings: Do not climb or lean over edges during wind or rain.
Do not block emergency exits with stored items.

records.title: Small tool safety routine
records.summary: A routine for hand tools, blades, handles, storage, and shared use without injuries.
records.content: Simple tools cause injuries when tired people use dull blades, cracked handles, missing guards, or bad lighting. Make one storage place, one repair pile, and one rule: damaged tools are labeled and not used as normal. Keep cutting edges covered and teach people to pass tools handle-first.
steps: Inspect handles and edges before work.
Work in light, stable space.
Label damaged tools immediately.
Store sharp tools covered.
Stop work when tiredness makes hands unsafe.
warnings: Do not use cracked handles or unstable ladders.
Do not let children handle sharp tools unsupervised.

records.title: Shoe and foot care station
records.summary: A shared foot-care station helps people inspect feet, dry footwear, change socks, and identify problems before walking ability is lost. It must separate clean and used items, protect privacy, and refer wounds or high-risk feet rather than performing invasive treatment.
records.content:
Core procedure:
1. Divide the station into clean seating, used-footwear drop, washing or wiping area, drying rack, and waste zone so traffic moves in one direction. 2. Admit one person per inspection place, explain the limits of the service, provide privacy, and clean hands before touching supplies or assisting another person. 3. Ask the person to remove one shoe and sock at a time; inspect the foot and shoe together for moisture, grit, pressure marks, wounds, swelling, odour, drainage, or damaged linings. 4. Provide clean socks, adjust or exchange footwear, and place reusable wet items in a clearly labelled drying route without mixing them with ready-to-issue stock. 5. Cover only minor wounds with appropriate clean materials; separate and refer anyone with infection signs, impaired circulation, severe pain, deep injury, or high-risk foot disease. 6. After each user, discard or segregate contaminated items, clean the seat and inspection surface, update stock and referral records, and reset the clean zone. Primary safety boundary: Do not let the station become a clinic for cutting calluses, opening blisters, treating deep wounds, or changing prescribed care; its role is inspection, hygiene, fit correction, simple protection, and referral. Fallback: When a full station cannot be separated, use individual kits at spaced seats and move sealed used items to a separate collection point.
materials: two-zone table for clean and used items
assorted clean socks and labelled footwear bins
single-person foot inspection light and mirror
sealed waste container and referral log
warnings: Do not let the station become a clinic for cutting calluses, opening blisters, treating deep wounds, or changing prescribed care; its role is inspection, hygiene, fit correction, simple protection, and referral.
Never return used socks, dressings, towels, or uncleaned footwear to the clean stock, and never share blades, needles, or opened topical products.
common_mistakes: Allowing clean and used footwear to cross on the same surface
Serving several people at one seat without cleaning between them
Issuing a different shoe size without checking standing fit and walking control
Recording stock use but not urgent referrals or follow-up time
alternatives: When a full station cannot be separated, use individual kits at spaced seats and move sealed used items to a separate collection point.
When footwear sizes are exhausted, prioritise pressure relief, dry socks, reduced walking, and transport while replacement pairs are sourced.
failure_signs: Clean and contaminated flows can no longer be kept apart
The waiting line prevents privacy, safe seating, or timely referral
Several users develop similar rash, drainage, odour, or wound symptoms suggesting a shared hygiene problem
when_not_to_use: Close the station when hand hygiene, surface cleaning, waste containment, privacy, or safe referral cannot be maintained.
Do not process a person with uncontrolled bleeding, severe infection signs, loss of circulation, major trauma, or another emergency before urgent care is arranged.
records.short_term: Set up one clean cycle, process one person at a time, disinfect shared surfaces, and record supplies that must be replaced.

records.content: Core sequence: 1) Reserve the cleanest cloth for wounds, infants, faces, and underwear instead of washing everything equally. 2) Air clothing in sun or moving air, then brush dry dirt away from cooking and sleeping areas. 3) Wash small high-contact items first: underwear, socks, masks, wound cloths, and pillow covers. 4) Separate contaminated flood, sewage, chemical, or animal-waste clothing until proper washing or disposal is possible.

records.title: Foot care during long walking
records.summary: Long walking can turn small pressure points, wet socks, grit, or poorly fitted footwear into blisters and loss of mobility. This card uses scheduled checks, drying, fit adjustment, and early stopping so a minor problem is not carried into a serious injury.
records.content:
Core procedure:
1. Before departure, inspect both feet and footwear, trim nothing aggressively, remove grit, confirm dry socks, and identify any existing numbness, wound, blister, or pressure point. 2. Wash or wipe gently when safe, dry carefully—especially between toes—and keep wet socks and footwear separate from clean replacements. 3. Check skin colour, temperature, swelling, cracks, blisters, cuts, drainage, pain, numbness, and the inside of each shoe for grit, folds, nails, or rough seams. 4. Correct the cause: loosen or re-lace pressure points, change to dry socks, smooth the insole, rest, and protect intact irritated skin without cutting or puncturing it. 5. Keep open wounds clean and covered with an appropriate clean dressing, avoid weight on a worsening injury, and seek qualified care for infection or impaired circulation signs. 6. Record the side and exact location of the problem, action taken, walking limit, recheck time, and whether the person has diabetes, poor circulation, loss of sensation, or another high-risk condition. Primary safety boundary: Do not cut calluses, dig into nails, drain or puncture blisters, apply unknown chemicals, or continue walking on rapidly worsening pain, swelling, colour change, numbness, or an open infected-looking wound. Fallback: If washing water is scarce, remove visible dirt with a clean slightly damp cloth, dry fully, and reserve clean water for wounds and drinking priorities.
materials: clean water when available or clean wipes
clean dressing supplies for minor intact-skin protection
mirror, light, and private seated inspection area
warnings: Do not cut calluses, dig into nails, drain or puncture blisters, apply unknown chemicals, or continue walking on rapidly worsening pain, swelling, colour change, numbness, or an open infected-looking wound.
People with diabetes, poor circulation, reduced sensation, immune suppression, or previous foot ulcers need a lower threshold for qualified medical review.
common_mistakes: Ignoring a hot spot until a blister forms
Putting clean socks back into wet or gritty footwear
Using shared blades, needles, creams, or towels
Forcing continued walking after gait, colour, sensation, or wound condition worsens
alternatives: If washing water is scarce, remove visible dirt with a clean slightly damp cloth, dry fully, and reserve clean water for wounds and drinking priorities.
If proper footwear is unavailable, reduce distance and load, pad pressure points without restricting circulation, and arrange transport or replacement footwear.
failure_signs: Spreading redness, warmth, swelling, pus, foul odour, fever, red streaks, or rapidly increasing pain
Blue, pale, black, very cold, or numb toes; inability to bear weight; deep puncture; uncontrolled bleeding; or suspected fracture
A blister, wound, or pressure area repeatedly worsens despite rest, drying, and fit correction
when_not_to_use: Do not rely on self-care for severe injury, spreading infection, circulation loss, deep puncture, contaminated wound, frostbite, burn, or a high-risk person with a new foot lesion.
Do not use a communal station while clean and contaminated items cannot be separated or while privacy, hand hygiene, and surface cleaning cannot be maintained.
records.short_term: Complete a foot and footwear check at the next safe stop, dry or change socks, correct fit, and shorten the route if symptoms are increasing.
records.long_term: Maintain footwear sizes, sock stocks, cleaning supplies, referral criteria, and a simple record of recurring fit or skin problems.
records.if_method_fails: Stop walking or station use, keep the foot clean and protected, reduce pressure, document the change, and arrange qualified assessment or transport.
records.environment_notes: In heat, cold, rain, or flood debris, shorten check intervals; never sacrifice balance or shelter from immediate hazards just to inspect a foot.

records.title: Smoke and dust clean-room plan
records.summary: A practical plan for reducing indoor smoke or dust exposure when outdoor air is poor.
records.content: When outdoor air is smoky or dusty, choose one room to keep cleaner. Close obvious gaps, reduce indoor burning, avoid sweeping dust into the air, and keep vulnerable people in the cleanest room. If filtration equipment exists, use it according to instructions. Do not use devices that create ozone indoors. Watch breathing comfort and seek medical help for severe symptoms.
steps: Choose a room with few gaps and low traffic.
Keep windows and doors closed when outdoor air is poor.
Avoid candles, smoking, frying, and unnecessary indoor dust.
Use damp cleaning instead of dry sweeping.
Track symptoms and official air guidance if available.
warnings: Do not block ventilation around fuel-burning appliances.
Do not ignore severe breathing trouble.

records.title: Cold exposure home routine
records.summary: A routine for clothing layers, warm room management, dry feet, warm drinks, and checks on vulnerable people.
records.content: Cold protection is more than adding one heavy coat. Layers, dry socks, wind blocking, warm shared rooms, safe heating, and regular checks work together. Keep feet dry, change wet clothes quickly, and keep people from lying directly on cold floors. If someone becomes confused, unusually sleepy, clumsy, or very cold to the touch, seek help and warm gradually without unsafe heat sources.
steps: Create one warm room.
Layer clothing without cutting circulation.
Keep socks and bedding dry.
Schedule warm drinks or meals when possible.

warnings: Do not use outdoor heaters indoors.
Do not sleep beside open flame.
Do not ignore confusion or extreme sleepiness in cold.

records.title: Apartment heat refuge plan
records.summary: A low-power plan for reducing heat exposure inside apartments and protecting vulnerable people.
records.content: Heat risk rises when rooms trap sun, air stops moving, people stop drinking, and vulnerable people are checked too late. Choose the coolest room, reduce direct sun, move activity to cooler hours, keep water visible, and check people at fixed times. Fans help only when conditions are suitable and power exists. If someone becomes confused, faint, very weak, or stops sweating in severe heat, seek urgent medical help.
steps: Identify the coolest room before midday.
Shade windows that receive direct sun.
Move chores to early morning or evening.
Check vulnerable people regularly.
Record water intake if someone is at risk.
warnings: Do not ignore confusion or fainting in heat.
Do not leave children, elderly people, sick people, or pets in hot closed spaces.

records.title: Room-in-room winter heat refuge
records.summary: Reduces occupied space during cold outages without unsafe indoor combustion.
records.content: Room-in-room winter heat refuge is a practical offline routine for cold shelter. Choose the smallest safe room away from broken windows, damp walls, and carbon monoxide risks. Block drafts with fabric while keeping required ventilation; never use charcoal, grills, or generators indoors. Create a sleeping zone away from cold floors using rugs, cardboard, or raised bedding. Group people by warmth needs while protecting privacy, illness separation, and mobility access. Check condensation, damp bedding, cold injuries, and candle/fire hazards every shift.

records.title: Summer shade and airflow retrofit
records.summary: Reduces indoor heat without blocking exits or trapping people.
records.content: Summer shade and airflow retrofit is a practical offline routine for heat shelter. Identify the coolest room by actual temperature, shade, night cooling, and safe airflow. Shade windows from the outside if safe because it stops sun before the glass. Use night flushing when outside air is cooler and daytime blocking when outside is hotter. Keep exits, stairs, and balcony doors usable during fire or earthquake. Set water, rest, and buddy checks for children, elderly people, workers, and heat-sensitive medicines.

records.title: Temporary roof tarp leak sequence
records.summary: Controls roof leaks while avoiding dangerous climbing during storms.
records.content: Temporary roof tarp leak sequence is a practical offline routine for roof leak control. During wind, lightning, or unstable roof conditions, manage water from inside instead of climbing. Move people, beds, medicines, batteries, documents, and dry food away from drip zones. Catch water and mark it as non-drinking unless assessed. Place external tarp only when weather, ladder, roof, and helper conditions are safe. Check ceiling sagging, cracks, electrical smell, mold, and slip hazards every shift.
steps: Catch water and mark it as non-drinking unless assessed.

records.title: Bicycle cargo repair and evacuation check
records.summary: Checks a bicycle before moving water, food, medicines, or evacuation bags.
records.content: Bicycle cargo repair and evacuation check is a practical offline routine for transport repair. Check brakes, tires, chain, steering, lights/reflectors, rack, and loose bolts before loading. Balance loads low and centered; keep bags away from wheels and brakes. Test ride empty and then with partial load before carrying critical supplies. Separate clean water/food from fuel, chemicals, trash, and dirty tools. Stop using the bicycle if braking, wobble, tire damage, or rider fatigue becomes unsafe.

records.title: Broken window weather seal and glass zone
records.summary: Handles glass, weather, privacy, and ventilation after a broken window.
records.content: Broken window weather seal and glass zone is a practical offline routine for window repair safety. Clear people and pets from the glass zone before sweeping. Pick large pieces with protection if available and place them in a rigid marked container. Sweep small shards with light from different angles and check shoes, bedding, and floor cracks. Cover the opening without sealing all ventilation when heat, illness, or cooking is an issue. Review after wind, rain, aftershocks, or children entering the room.

records.title: Building collapse: immediate movement and safe exit decision
records.summary: A rapid decision card for people inside or beside a newly damaged building: protect the head and airway, avoid falling hazards, leave only by a safer route, and never re-enter for property.
records.content: Use the materials as a compact field kit. Work through the steps in order, pause whenever a warning or stop condition applies, and write down the outcome so another person can continue safely.
steps: Protect your head and neck, move away from glass, shelves, façades, and visibly sagging structural parts.
Check the nearest route without using lifts; if smoke, fire, exposed wiring, gas odour, or falling debris blocks it, choose a safer shelter point and call 112.
When a usable route exists, leave calmly, help only without entering unstable zones, and move to an open assembly area away from walls and power lines.
Account for people, report the exact address and observed hazards, and prevent anyone from re-entering until authorities declare it safe.
warnings: Aftershocks and secondary collapse can occur without warning.
Do not touch switches or create sparks when gas is suspected.

records.title: Damaged building exclusion zone and re-entry boundary
records.summary: A simple perimeter system that keeps residents and helpers away from collapse, glass, fire, electricity, gas, and falling-object zones until qualified inspection.
steps: Observe only from a safe distance and note leaning walls, loose façades, broken glass, smoke, water flow, utility damage, and blocked access.
Set a conservative boundary beyond the likely fall distance and keep emergency access lanes open.
Post one clear message at every approach: no entry, identified hazards, time set, responsible contact, and official service called.
Maintain an entry log only for authorized responders and move the boundary outward if conditions worsen.
warnings: Tape is a warning, not structural protection.
Never allow a quick property-retrieval visit before official clearance.

records.title: Missing-person sighting verification and duplicate-report merge
records.summary: A controlled log for comparing sightings by time, place, direction, witness reliability, and distinguishing details before passing a consolidated report to authorities.
steps: Give every incoming sighting a unique number and record the witness’s direct observations separately from conclusions or rumours.
Compare exact time, position, direction, clothing, companions, vehicle, speech, gait, and other distinguishing details against the verified description.
Plot plausible sightings in time order, mark contradictions and duplicates, and contact the witness again only through the designated coordinator.
Send authorities a concise consolidated update that preserves original forms and clearly labels confirmed, plausible, conflicting, and disproved reports.
warnings: Do not redirect an official search from an unverified social-media claim.
Do not reveal the missing person’s private details beyond operational need.

records.title: Untrained volunteer search-team safety boundary
records.summary: A strict boundary for community volunteers: operate only under authority coordination, in low-risk assigned areas, with check-in, communications, stop rules, and no technical rescue.
records.content: Use the materials as a compact field kit.
steps: Report to the official incident lead or police and accept only a defined low-risk task, area, time window, reporting channel, and return point.

Observe and report from safe ground; mark locations without moving evidence, entering structures, approaching cliffs, water, fire, utilities, hazardous materials, or aggressive animals.

records.title: Vehicle trapped by rising floodwater
records.summary: Recognize the need to abandon an immobilized vehicle early and move away from water without attempting a crossing.
records.content: Action sequence: Never drive into a flooded road, torrent, underpass, or moving water. If the vehicle becomes immobilized and water is rising, call 112, release seat belts, help children or dependent passengers, and leave when a safe exit is possible. Move to stable higher ground away from the water path, bridges, banks, and fallen wires. Report the exact vehicle location and number of people; do not return for property. Safety boundary: Do not enter moving floodwater on foot to reach a road or vehicle. Do not stay inside merely because the vehicle feels heavy or protected.
materials: seat-belt cutter and window tool stored accessibly
steps: Never drive into a flooded road, torrent, underpass, or moving water.
warnings: Do not enter moving floodwater on foot to reach a road or vehicle.

records.title: Stranded vehicle in snow or frost
records.summary: Conserve heat, maintain ventilation, make the vehicle visible, and avoid carbon monoxide exposure while arranging rescue.
records.content: Action sequence: Call for help with road, direction, landmarks, vehicle description, occupants, fuel, and medical needs. Stay with the vehicle unless a clearly visible safe building is very close and authorities advise movement. If the engine is used, first ensure the exhaust outlet remains completely clear and maintain safe ventilation; use short intervals to conserve fuel. Layer clothing, keep people dry, move fingers and toes gently, and check each other for confusion or worsening cold stress. Safety boundary: Do not sleep with the engine running continuously. Do not walk into poor visibility, traffic, or unfamiliar terrain without a confirmed safe destination.
steps: Call for help with road, direction, landmarks, vehicle description, occupants, fuel, and medical needs.
warnings: Do not sleep with the engine running continuously.
common_mistakes: Do not sleep with the engine running continuously.

records.title: Wildfire evacuation vehicle loading order
records.summary: Load people, essential medicines, communication, animals, documents, and water in a fixed order so departure is not delayed by possessions.
records.content: Action sequence: Park facing the escape direction when risk rises and keep enough fuel or charge for the planned route and diversion. Load dependent people and mobility aids first, then medicines, communication, animal control, identity documents, and water. Leave at the earliest official instruction or when the route, visibility, smoke, or household ability begins to deteriorate. Use the official route and keep windows closed and ventilation set to recirculate when smoke is present, if the vehicle system allows it. Safety boundary: Do not delay departure to load furniture, tools, fuel containers, or replaceable property. Do not drive toward smoke or fire to inspect it or retrieve another vehicle.
steps: Park facing the escape direction when risk rises and keep enough fuel or charge for the planned route and diversion.
warnings: Do not delay departure to load furniture, tools, fuel containers, or replaceable property.

records.title: Pedestrian evacuation route with no private vehicle
records.summary: Plan realistic walking, public-transport, neighbour, taxi, municipal, and responder options for households without a car.
records.content: Action sequence: Mark two walkable routes that avoid torrents, dense vegetation, tunnels, steep unstable slopes, and roads without safe pedestrian space. Identify bus stops, taxi contacts, neighbours, municipal assistance, accessible transport, and safe pickup points before an alert. Set a lower departure threshold because walking and assisted transport take longer than driving. Carry only what can be moved safely while keeping hands available for balance, children, or mobility aids. Safety boundary: Do not choose a route simply because it is shortest; hazard exposure and accessibility matter more. Do not wait until smoke, water, darkness, or crowding makes assisted transport impossible.
steps: Mark two walkable routes that avoid torrents, dense vegetation, tunnels, steep unstable slopes, and roads without safe pedestrian space.
warnings: Do not choose a route simply because it is shortest; hazard exposure and accessibility matter more.

records.title: Vehicle emergency kit for Greek summer heat
records.summary: Build a heat-safe vehicle kit and storage routine that does not leave water, medicines, batteries, or people in dangerous temperatures.
records.content: Action sequence: Keep a permanent non-medical kit, but bring temperature-sensitive medicines, power banks, and drinking water from indoors for each trip. Plan fuel or charge, shaded stops, roadside assistance, and a contact who knows the route. If stranded, move occupants to the safest cool location available, use shade and airflow, and call for help before symptoms worsen. Inspect containers, batteries, adhesives, food, and plastic items after prolonged heat exposure and replace damaged stock. Safety boundary: Never leave a child, dependent adult, or animal in a parked vehicle, even briefly. Do not store medicines or swollen, leaking, or damaged batteries in a hot vehicle.

records.title: Apartment stairwell smoke decision
records.summary: Helps a resident decide whether a stairwell is usable when smoke, heat, alarms, or fire smell appear in a block of flats.
records.content: Core sequence: 1) Feel the door and handle with the back of the hand before opening even a few centimeters. 2) If smoke enters from the stairwell, close the door, block gaps, move to a window or balcony, and call 112. 3) If the stairwell is clear, descend calmly without using lifts and close doors behind you. 4) Mark the flat as occupied only if it can be done without entering smoke. Stop point: Do not enter a smoky stairwell to rescue belongings, pets, chargers, or documents. Main warnings: Do not open a hot door to look; heat behind the door is already useful information. Do not use a lift during a fire alarm or smoke event.
steps: Feel the door and handle with the back of the hand before opening even a few centimeters.
If smoke enters from the stairwell, close the door, block gaps, move to a window or balcony, and call 112.
If the stairwell is clear, descend calmly without using lifts and close doors behind you.
Mark the flat as occupied only if it can be done without entering smoke.
warnings: Do not open a hot door to look; heat behind the door is already useful information.
Do not use a lift during a fire alarm or smoke event.
common_mistakes: Running downstairs into smoke can trap the resident below the fire floor.
Leaving the flat unlocked without keys can prevent re-entry if the stairwell becomes unusable.
alternatives: If voice calls fail, send a short message with floor, side of building, number of people, smoke level, and visible window.
If balcony air is also smoky, stay low, seal the room, and wait for official direction.
failure_signs: Coughing, heat on the door, dark smoke under the frame, or confusion appear.
The stairwell light fails and the smell becomes stronger between floors.
when_not_to_use: Do not enter a smoky stairwell to rescue belongings, pets, chargers, or documents.
Do not break windows unless responders instruct it or smoke makes staying impossible.
records.short_term: Keep keys, shoes, phone, and a cloth reachable from the sleeping area.
records.long_term: Learn two exits, floor numbering, and the safest window or balcony signal point before any fire.
records.if_method_fails: If the decision fails, close the last safe door, call 112, describe smoke and floor, and stop self-evacuation attempts.
records.environment_notes: Older buildings may lack alarms or clear floor signs; use doors, light wells, balconies, and known neighbors as reference points.

records.title: Safe refrigerator and freezer outage log
records.summary: Preserve cold by keeping doors closed and record outage time and temperature evidence before deciding what food or medicine can be used.
records.content: Action sequence: Write the exact time power failed and avoid opening appliance doors merely to check. Record any thermometer reading, door opening, generator transfer, restored-power time, and official food or medicine advice. Separate decisions for food, refrigerated medicine, breast milk, and other temperature-sensitive items. Label uncertain items and obtain authoritative guidance before use; discard items that are officially considered unsafe. Safety boundary: Do not taste food to judge safety. Do not apply general food timing rules to medicines; obtain product-specific advice.
steps: Write the exact time power failed and avoid opening appliance doors merely to check.
warnings: Do not taste food to judge safety.
common_mistakes: Do not taste food to judge safety.

records.title: Carbon monoxide prevention during an outage
records.summary: Prevent invisible carbon monoxide buildup by keeping all fuel-burning devices outdoors and away from occupied openings.
records.content: Action sequence: Use generators, grills, charcoal, pressure washers, and other fuel-burning engines outdoors only and far from doors, windows, and vents. Point exhaust away from occupied areas and prevent rain exposure without enclosing the engine. Test carbon-monoxide alarms and move everyone to fresh air immediately if an alarm sounds or symptoms such as headache, dizziness, weakness, nausea, chest pain, or confusion appear. Call 112 from a safe outdoor location and do not re-enter until professionals say it is safe. Safety boundary: Never use a gas oven or stovetop to heat the home. Never run a generator in a home, garage, basement, balcony enclosure, shed attached to the home, or near occupied openings.
steps: Use generators, grills, charcoal, pressure washers, and other fuel-burning engines outdoors only and far from doors, windows, and vents.
warnings: Never use a gas oven or stovetop to heat the home.

records.title: Utility shutoff identification without unsafe operation
records.summary: Label water, electricity, gas, and fuel controls and define who may operate them so an emergency does not become a live-utility accident.
records.content: Action sequence: Photograph and sketch each main control, meter, access route, tool requirement, and provider emergency number. Ask qualified providers which controls a resident may safely operate and which require a professional. Keep the access area dry, clear, lit, and free from stored objects. After any shutoff, label who acted, why, when, and who must inspect before restart. Safety boundary: Do not touch wet, damaged, sparking, hot, gas-affected, or unknown utility equipment. Do not restore gas or electricity after damage without the required qualified inspection.
steps: Photograph and sketch each main control, meter, access route, tool requirement, and provider emergency number.
warnings: Do not touch wet, damaged, sparking, hot, gas-affected, or unknown utility equipment.

records.title: Apartment stairwell emergency inspection from a safe position
records.summary: Check whether the normal exit has smoke, heat, water, debris, structural damage, or crowding before committing the household to it.
records.content: Action sequence: From the protected side, look, listen, and smell for smoke, heat, gas, water, falling material, alarms, and people moving. Test a door for unusual heat without opening into a suspected fire and keep the household behind the safe boundary. Use the stairs only when they are clear and authorities have not restricted them; never rely on a lift during fire. If the route is unsafe, close the boundary, call 112, give the floor and apartment, and move to the planned protected waiting location. Safety boundary: Do not open a door into visible smoke, strong heat, or suspected fire. Do not enter a damaged stairwell to retrieve property or check another floor.
steps: From the protected side, look, listen, and smell for smoke, heat, gas, water, falling material, alarms, and people moving.
warnings: Do not open a door into visible smoke, strong heat, or suspected fire.

records.summary: Allocate limited charging to emergency communication, medical needs, lighting, and verified information before entertainment or convenience.
records.content: Action sequence: List every device, owner, purpose, current charge, minimum safe reserve, charging time, and compatible source. Rank life-sustaining medical devices and 112 communication first, followed by lighting, radio, navigation, and household coordination. Use scheduled charging windows and airplane or low-power modes outside those windows. Inspect for swelling, leakage, heat, odour, damaged cables, or wet connectors before each charge. Safety boundary: Do not charge a damaged, wet, swollen, leaking, or unusually hot battery. Do not connect unknown adapters or overload an improvised power source.
steps: List every device, owner, purpose, current charge, minimum safe reserve, charging time, and compatible source.
warnings: Do not charge a damaged, wet, swollen, leaking, or unusually hot battery.

records.content: Core sequence: 1) Attach a large label to the valve with closed time, reason, affected rooms, and who may reopen it. 2) Tell all household members where safe drinking water is stored before closing the valve. 3) Keep a small test container ready for first reopening only after the leak or contamination concern is resolved. 4) Remove the label only when the responsible person confirms no active leak, electrical wet area, or official advisory remains.
