source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/01 - Observe sun, wind and access before planting.json

records.title: Observe sun, wind and access before planting
records.subcategory: Observe sun, wind and access before planting
records.summary: Map the growing area before spending seed or labour.
steps: Observe the site at morning, midday and late afternoon; note direct sun, reflected heat and deep shade.
Mark strong-wind corridors, roof runoff, animal access, trip hazards and places that remain waterlogged.
Place frequently harvested crops near safe daily access and water.
Start with one small test bed or two containers and record results for two weeks.
Expand only where plants receive suitable light and drainage.

source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/02 - Build a realistic garden water budget.json

records.title: Build a realistic garden water budget
records.subcategory: Build a realistic garden water budget
records.summary: Match planted area to water that can be supplied through the hottest period.
steps: List reliable water sources and separate drinking-water reserves from garden water.
Measure how much one normal watering uses rather than estimating.
Prioritise seedlings, recently transplanted plants and high-value crops during shortage.
Reduce bare soil with mulch and group plants with similar water needs.
Keep an emergency reduction plan: fewer containers, smaller beds and lower-water crops.

source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/03 - Choose crops by food value, time and risk.json

records.title: Choose crops by food value, time and risk
records.subcategory: Choose crops by food value, time and risk
records.summary: Balance quick harvests, reliable staples, nutrition and storage value.
steps: Write the household goal: fresh greens, flavour, calories, protein contribution, storage or seed continuity.
Score each candidate crop for local suitability, days to harvest, water, space, skill and preservation needs.
Include fast crops and slower high-yield crops instead of depending on only one type.
Prefer crops the household will actually eat and can prepare safely.
Review yield and labour after harvest; replace poor performers next cycle.

source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/04 - Mediterranean four-season growing plan.json

records.title: Mediterranean four-season growing plan
records.summary: Plan around cool wet periods, spring acceleration, dry heat and autumn recovery.
steps: Divide the local year by actual temperature, rainfall and heat exposure, not calendar names alone.
Use cooler periods for many leafy greens, peas, broad beans, brassicas, onions and roots where locally suitable.
Use warming periods for tomatoes, peppers, eggplants, beans, cucumbers and squash after cold risk passes.
During extreme summer heat protect soil, provide shade where appropriate and avoid starting more than water can support.
Use autumn to restart cool-season crops and review which varieties tolerated local conditions.

source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/05 - Succession sowing for continuous harvest.json

records.title: Succession sowing for continuous harvest
records.summary: Spread harvest and failure risk by sowing small batches at intervals.
steps: Choose crops suited to repeated sowing, such as salad leaves, radish, beans or herbs in the appropriate season.
Sow a small labelled batch instead of the entire packet.
Record emergence and expected harvest; sow the next batch only if weather and water remain suitable.
Stop sowing when the crop will mature in unsuitable heat or cold.
Keep one batch as a reserve when pests or weather damage another.

source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/06 - Simple crop rotation and garden log.json

records.title: Simple crop rotation and garden log
records.subcategory: Simple crop rotation and garden log
records.summary: Use records to avoid repeating the same crop family and the same mistakes.
steps: Draw a basic map and label each bed or container.
Record crop family, planting date, source, fertilisation, pest problems and harvest.
Where space allows, avoid planting the same crop family in the same soil every cycle.
Rotate with crops having different rooting and nutrient patterns; include soil-building cover where practical.
Keep rotation flexible when container mix is replaced or disease history requires a stricter response.

source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/07 - Basic soil assessment before planting.json

records.title: Basic soil assessment before planting
records.summary: Check drainage, texture, compaction, organic matter and contamination history.
steps: Review the site history and stop if there is credible contamination risk.
After rain or watering, note whether water infiltrates or remains pooled.
Take samples from several points for a representative soil test where available.
Loosen compacted surface carefully without damaging buried utilities.
Amend from test results and plant a small trial before treating the whole area.

source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/08 - Build a balanced home compost pile.json

records.title: Build a balanced home compost pile
records.subcategory: Build a balanced home compost pile
records.summary: Turn suitable kitchen and garden material into a stable soil amendment.
steps: Choose a drained location away from direct contact with food preparation areas.
Alternate moist nitrogen-rich material with dry carbon-rich material; cut bulky pieces smaller.
Keep the pile damp like a wrung sponge, not waterlogged.
Mix or turn when it compacts, smells strongly or stops breaking down.
Use only when material is dark, crumbly, earthy-smelling and no longer recognisably fresh.

source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/09 - What must stay out of home compost.json

records.title: What must stay out of home compost
records.subcategory: What must stay out of home compost
records.summary: Prevent pathogens, pests, chemicals and persistent weeds entering the food garden.
steps: Exclude pet and human waste, nappies and sewage-contaminated material.
For simple home systems exclude meat, fish, bones, dairy, fats and oily cooked food that attract pests.
Exclude chemically treated wood, glossy or plastic-coated material, ash of unknown origin and pesticide-contaminated plants.
Keep diseased plants and mature invasive weed seed out unless the system is managed to destroy them reliably.
When uncertain, dispose through the appropriate local waste route instead of composting.

source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/10 - Small-space vermicomposting.json

records.title: Small-space vermicomposting
records.summary: Use a ventilated worm bin for selected food scraps where outdoor compost is impractical.
steps: Use a lidded ventilated bin with moist bedding and composting worms suitable for the system.
Add small amounts of chopped fruit and vegetable scraps, coffee grounds and plain plant material.
Bury new food under bedding and wait until most is consumed before adding more.
Correct odour or flies by removing unsuitable food, reducing feed and adding dry bedding.
Harvest finished castings separately and introduce them gradually to potting mix or soil.

source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/11 - Mulch for moisture and soil protection.json

records.title: Mulch for moisture and soil protection
records.subcategory: Mulch for moisture and soil protection
records.summary: Cover bare soil while preventing stem rot, pests and contaminated inputs.
steps: Water and weed before applying clean mulch.
Use a moderate loose layer of straw, shredded leaves or another locally suitable material.
Leave a clear ring around stems and trunks to maintain airflow.
Inspect beneath mulch for slugs, rodents, persistent wetness or fungal growth.
Top up only after checking soil moisture; do not create a permanently saturated layer.

source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/12 - Recognise and reduce salt buildup.json

records.title: Recognise and reduce salt buildup
records.summary: Manage crusting and plant stress in containers or irrigated soil without guessing.
steps: Look for white crust, burned leaf edges, stunted growth and repeated wilting despite moist soil.
Check drainage first and review fertiliser dose and irrigation-water quality.
Stop unnecessary fertiliser and remove visible surface deposits without damaging roots.
Where drainage and water quality permit, leach containers thoroughly and let them drain completely.
Replace severely degraded mix and seek a water or soil test when the problem returns.

source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/13 - Build and fill a safe raised bed.json

records.title: Build and fill a safe raised bed
records.subcategory: Build and fill a safe raised bed
records.summary: Create a drainable growing area where native soil is poor or access is limited.
steps: Choose a stable level location with suitable sun, water access and no buried utility conflict.
Use durable untreated or food-garden-appropriate materials; avoid unknown reclaimed chemical containers or treated timber.
Provide depth suitable for intended roots and a route for excess water to escape.
Fill with a known clean soil-compost blend rather than pure compost.
Settle, water, check drainage and plant a small test area before full use.

source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/14 - Choose safe containers and drainage.json

records.title: Choose safe containers and drainage
records.summary: Match container volume, material and drainage to the crop.
steps: Use a structurally sound container with known previous use and enough root volume.
Create several unobstructed drainage holes and raise the base so water can escape.
Use clean potting mix; garden soil alone often compacts in containers.
Leave watering space below the rim and secure tall containers against wind or tipping.
Before planting, wet the mix and confirm that drainage is even rather than one blocked channel.

source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/15 - Prepare a practical container growing mix.json

records.title: Prepare a practical container growing mix
records.subcategory: Prepare a practical container growing mix
records.summary: Use a light, clean, moisture-retentive but drainable medium.
steps: Start with labelled commercial potting mix or known clean components intended for containers.
Add mature compost in a moderate proportion rather than filling the container with compost alone.
Avoid dense clay soil, rubble, unknown fill and materials contaminated by chemicals or animal waste.
Moisten before planting and break dry clumps without crushing all pore space.
Replace or refresh mix when drainage collapses, disease persists or salt buildup cannot be corrected.

source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/16 - Water the root zone, not the calendar.json

records.title: Water the root zone, not the calendar
records.subcategory: Water the root zone, not the calendar
records.summary: Decide from soil moisture, plant stage and weather rather than a fixed daily habit.
steps: Check moisture below the surface with a finger, small trowel or moisture observation at several points.
Water slowly until the active root zone is wet; stop when runoff or deep pooling begins.
Water seedlings and new transplants more frequently but in controlled amounts while roots establish.
Prefer morning where practical so foliage and surfaces can dry.
After heat or wind, inspect plants and soil before adding more water; wilting can also come from root damage or saturation.

source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/17 - Set up and inspect simple drip irrigation.json

records.title: Set up and inspect simple drip irrigation
records.subcategory: Set up and inspect simple drip irrigation
records.summary: Deliver water near roots while finding leaks and blocked emitters early.
steps: Use a filter and pressure control appropriate to the water source and components.
Lay lines where emitters serve actual root zones, not empty soil.
Run the system while watching every section for leaks, spray, blockage and uneven flow.
Measure output from several emitters for the same time and correct large differences.
Inspect weekly and after repairs; automation does not remove the need to check soil moisture.

source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/18 - Protect edible crops during extreme heat.json

records.title: Protect edible crops during extreme heat
records.subcategory: Protect edible crops during extreme heat
records.summary: Reduce root-zone heat and water loss without trapping stagnant humid air.
steps: Check official heat forecasts and inspect containers that heat faster than ground soil.
Water the root zone before peak heat when soil is genuinely dry.
Use mulch and temporary shade cloth that still allows ventilation; do not wrap plants in plastic.
Move portable containers out of reflected wall or pavement heat.
Delay transplanting, heavy pruning and strong fertilisation until stress passes.

source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/19 - Create a useful seed inventory.json

records.title: Create a useful seed inventory
records.summary: Track identity, age, storage and remaining quantity before an emergency.
steps: Label each packet with crop, variety, source, harvest or purchase year and treatment warning.
Store cool, dry and dark in sealed, clearly separated containers.
Keep seed for food production separate from grain intended for eating.
Test a small sample from older lots and record germination before planning the bed.
Use oldest viable seed first while retaining a protected reserve.

source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/20 - Paper-towel seed germination test.json

records.title: Paper-towel seed germination test
records.summary: Estimate viability with a labelled small sample before using scarce space.
steps: Count a known number of seeds, commonly 10 or more, and record the lot.
Place them in a moist, not dripping, clean paper towel inside a loose container or bag.
Keep at the crop-appropriate temperature and check daily for mould and sprouting.
Count normally germinated seeds at the expected interval and calculate the percentage.
Use a higher sowing rate for moderately reduced viability; replace lots with very poor or mouldy performance.

source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/21 - Clean seed-starting routine.json

records.title: Clean seed-starting routine
records.summary: Reduce damping-off and weak growth through hygiene, light, airflow and measured moisture.
steps: Clean reusable trays and use fresh clean seed-starting mix.
Sow at the depth and spacing on the seed instructions; label immediately.
Moisten evenly without leaving trays standing in dirty water.
Provide sufficient light and gentle airflow as soon as seedlings emerge.
Remove collapsed or mouldy seedlings, isolate the tray and correct excess moisture or crowding.

source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/22 - Choose direct sowing or transplanting.json

records.title: Choose direct sowing or transplanting
records.summary: Use the method that protects the crop’s roots and fits the season.
steps: Direct-sow crops that resent root disturbance or are normally grown closely in place, following packet guidance.
Start slow warm-season crops indoors only when adequate light, space and later outdoor conditions exist.
Do not keep seedlings so long that roots circle heavily or plants become pale and stretched.
Prepare the final bed before moving seedlings and water the root ball.
Record which method produced faster establishment and lower loss locally.

source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/23 - Harden seedlings before transplanting.json

records.title: Harden seedlings before transplanting
records.summary: Acclimatise indoor-grown plants gradually to sun, wind and outdoor temperature.
steps: Begin several days before transplanting during mild weather.
Place seedlings outdoors first in sheltered shade for a short period.
Increase time and gentle sun exposure gradually while monitoring moisture.
Bring plants back or protect them during strong wind, cold, storms or extreme heat.
Transplant when plants remain firm and healthy after a normal outdoor period.

source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/24 - Leafy greens in beds and containers.json

records.title: Leafy greens in beds and containers
records.subcategory: Leafy greens in beds and containers
records.summary: Grow quick leaves with cool-season timing, steady moisture and repeated harvest.
steps: Choose lettuce, chard, spinach-like greens or local varieties suited to the current temperature.
Sow shallowly in clean fine soil and thin early so leaves receive airflow.
Keep moisture even without permanent saturation; shade may extend harvest during warming weather.
Harvest outer clean leaves or cut at the recommended stage while the plant is crisp.
Remove bolting, bitter or diseased plants and start a new small sowing in a better window.

source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/25 - Carrots, radishes and other root crops.json

records.title: Carrots, radishes and other root crops
records.subcategory: Carrots, radishes and other root crops
records.summary: Produce straight usable roots in loose, stone-free soil with timely thinning.
steps: Prepare a deep loose surface without fresh clumps of manure or large stones.
Direct-sow evenly at the packet depth and keep the surface gently moist until emergence.
Thin without delay so roots do not compete; water afterwards to reduce disturbance.
Keep shoulders covered where the crop requires it and control weeds while small.
Harvest sample roots first and avoid leaving them until they become woody, split or pest-damaged.

source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/26 - Peas and beans for a small garden.json

records.title: Peas and beans for a small garden
records.subcategory: Peas and beans for a small garden
records.summary: Use the correct season, support and harvest stage for productive legumes.
steps: Choose cool-season peas or warm-season beans according to local conditions and variety instructions.
Direct-sow into drained soil and avoid repeatedly saturating seed before emergence.
Install support before climbing types become tangled.
Inspect flowers and young pods during heat, drought and pest pressure; correct water stress at the root zone.
Pick green pods frequently or let dry-bean types mature fully and dry safely before storage.

source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/27 - Tomato growing and support.json

records.title: Tomato growing and support
records.summary: Manage transplanting, support, watering and disease observation for tomatoes.
steps: Use healthy hardened plants or start seed early enough for the local warm season.
Plant after damaging cold risk, with adequate root volume and immediate stake, cage or trellis support.
Water deeply and consistently at soil level; large wet-dry swings can damage fruit and roots.
Maintain airflow, remove leaves touching soil when appropriate and disinfect tools between suspect plants.
Harvest at the intended ripeness and remove fallen or diseased fruit promptly.

source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/28 - Peppers and eggplants.json

records.title: Peppers and eggplants
records.summary: Grow warm-season fruiting crops with early establishment and steady heat management.
steps: Start with healthy transplants when the local warm season is long enough and nights are no longer cold.
Provide full suitable light, warm soil and enough container or bed volume.
Keep root-zone moisture steady while avoiding waterlogged soil.
Support heavy branches and inspect leaf undersides for mites, aphids and whiteflies.
Harvest with clean cutters to avoid tearing branches; record which varieties set fruit during local heat.

source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/29 - Cucumbers and summer squash.json

records.title: Cucumbers and summer squash
records.summary: Provide space, pollination access, steady water and frequent harvest.
steps: Direct-sow or transplant only after soil and weather are suitably warm.
Give vines space or a strong trellis and avoid crushing the main stem.
Water near roots and keep leaves as dry as practical to reduce disease pressure.
Protect flowering access for pollinators and avoid unnecessary insecticide use during bloom.
Harvest frequently at useful size; oversized fruit slows continued production and may be poor quality.

source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/30 - Potatoes in beds or large containers.json

records.title: Potatoes in beds or large containers
records.subcategory: Potatoes in beds or large containers
records.summary: Grow potatoes from suitable seed material while preventing light exposure and rot.
steps: Use certified or otherwise trusted disease-free seed potatoes rather than unknown discarded tubers.
Plant in loose drained soil with enough depth and spacing.
As stems grow, hill clean soil or suitable medium around them without burying all foliage.
Keep developing tubers covered from light; green tubers are not food.
Harvest after the intended maturity in dry conditions where possible and cure only sound tubers before dark ventilated storage.

source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/31 - Onions and garlic.json

records.title: Onions and garlic
records.summary: Use clean planting material, weed control and correct curing for storage bulbs.
steps: Choose seed, sets or cloves suited to local day length and planting season.
Plant in loose drained soil with the top depth recommended for the material.
Keep weed competition low because narrow leaves shade soil poorly.
Reduce irrigation as bulbs mature according to crop condition and local weather.
Harvest when mature, cure in a dry ventilated shaded place and store only firm undamaged bulbs.

source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/32 - Mediterranean culinary herbs.json

records.title: Mediterranean culinary herbs
records.summary: Grow useful herbs without overwatering drought-tolerant species.
steps: Select correctly identified culinary species such as oregano, thyme, rosemary, sage, parsley, basil or mint.
Separate plants by water need; basil and parsley generally differ from woody Mediterranean herbs.
Use sharply drained soil for drought-tolerant woody herbs and avoid permanently wet roots.
Keep invasive spreaders such as mint in controlled containers where needed.
Harvest clean healthy growth before severe stress and never substitute a wild plant without positive identification.

source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/33 - Strawberries in small spaces.json

records.title: Strawberries in small spaces
records.summary: Manage crowns, runners, moisture and fruit cleanliness in beds or containers.
steps: Use healthy plants and set the crown at the soil surface rather than burying or exposing roots.
Provide good drainage, suitable sun and steady moisture during flowering and fruiting.
Keep fruit off bare wet soil with clean mulch or an appropriate support.
Remove diseased fruit and leaves promptly; control runners when they overcrowd the container.
Harvest fully coloured sound fruit into a clean shallow container and cool it promptly.

source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/34 - Weekly crop scouting routine.json

records.title: Weekly crop scouting routine
records.category: Food growing · Pest and disease control
records.summary: Find small problems before they become crop-wide failures.
steps: Inspect the same route at least weekly and more often during rapid growth or outbreaks.
Check new growth, leaf undersides, stems, soil line, flowers and fruit.
Record affected crop, exact location, pattern, weather and number of plants.
Photograph or isolate a sample for identification before choosing treatment.
Recheck after any action and stop ineffective treatment rather than repeating it blindly.

source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/35 - Aphids, whiteflies and mites.json

records.title: Aphids, whiteflies and mites
records.category: Food growing · Pest and disease control
records.summary: Use identification, water management, physical removal and beneficial insects before escalation.
steps: Confirm the pest on leaf undersides with a hand lens when possible.
Isolate heavily infested container plants and remove only severely damaged growth.
Use a controlled water spray where the plant tolerates it, avoiding disease-promoting prolonged wetness.
Reduce excess nitrogen and protect beneficial insects; avoid broad-spectrum treatment without need.
If a labelled product is necessary, cover the full target area exactly as the label directs and observe the harvest interval.

source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/36 - Slugs, snails and chewing caterpillars.json

records.title: Slugs, snails and chewing caterpillars
records.category: Food growing · Pest and disease control
records.summary: Combine night inspection, barriers and targeted removal.
steps: Identify feeding pattern and inspect at dusk, night or early morning when the pest is active.
Remove hiding boards, dense debris and weeds immediately beside vulnerable seedlings.
Hand-pick safely with gloves or use crop covers that do not trap pests underneath.
Check covers after wind and remove them when pollination access is required.
Use only a product explicitly labelled for the crop and pest, and protect children, pets and wildlife.

source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/37 - Reduce fungal disease pressure.json

records.title: Reduce fungal disease pressure
records.category: Food growing · Pest and disease control
records.summary: Use spacing, airflow, clean watering and sanitation before relying on sprays.
steps: Space and prune only as appropriate for the crop to improve airflow.
Water soil rather than leaves and prefer timing that allows surfaces to dry.
Remove infected fallen material and do not move it through clean beds or compost unless safe processing is certain.
Disinfect tools between suspect plants and avoid working through wet foliage.
Seek identification when symptoms spread; different pathogens require different responses.

source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/38 - Quarantine new plants and seed stock.json

records.title: Quarantine new plants and seed stock
records.category: Food growing · Pest and disease control
records.subcategory: Quarantine new plants and seed stock
records.summary: Prevent imported pests and disease from entering the main garden.
steps: Buy or exchange only legally permitted, labelled plant material from a traceable source.
Inspect roots, stems, leaf undersides and growing medium before bringing material near established crops.
Keep new live plants separately for an observation period appropriate to the risk.
Use separate tools and avoid runoff from quarantine into the main area.
Destroy or report suspicious regulated pests according to official plant-health instructions rather than distributing the material.

source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/39 - Pesticide label and pre-harvest safety.json

records.title: Pesticide label and pre-harvest safety
records.category: Food growing · Pest and disease control
records.summary: Treat the legal label as the controlling instruction for any crop-protection product.
steps: Confirm the exact crop and target pest are listed; a product for another crop is not automatically suitable.
Read dose, mixing, application limits, protective equipment, re-entry and environmental restrictions before opening.
Measure with dedicated labelled equipment and prevent drift to people, animals, water and neighbouring crops.
Record date, product, rate, treated area and the required pre-harvest interval.
Do not harvest or distribute produce until the full interval and all label requirements are satisfied.

source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/40 - Clean harvest and field handling.json

records.title: Clean harvest and field handling
records.summary: Keep soil, damaged produce, chemicals and dirty containers away from sound food.
steps: Harvest with clean hands and clean food-contact tools into clean containers.
Keep containers off manure, pesticide-storage floors, fuel areas and dirty vehicle surfaces.
Separate bruised, cut, pest-damaged or visibly diseased produce for immediate assessment.
Move harvested food out of sun and heat promptly.
Wash produce under safe running water when appropriate; do not wash it with soap, bleach or household detergent.

source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/41 - Harvest, use-first and loss log.json

records.title: Harvest, use-first and loss log
records.summary: Turn garden output into reliable meals and better planting decisions.
steps: Record crop, bed, date, usable weight or count and visible damage.
Mark what must be eaten first, chilled, frozen, dried or otherwise preserved.
Keep seed-saving produce separate and clearly labelled.
Record storage losses and the reason: heat, moisture, bruising, pests, delay or processing failure.
Use actual edible yield, not planted area, when planning the next cycle.

source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/42 - Short-term cooling and refrigerator storage.json

records.title: Short-term cooling and refrigerator storage
records.summary: Cool suitable produce promptly while controlling condensation and cross-contamination.
steps: Remove field heat as soon as practical using the storage conditions suitable for that crop.
Use clean breathable or moisture-controlling packaging instead of sealing wet produce blindly.
Keep raw animal products below and separate from ready-to-eat garden produce.
Label harvest or preparation date and rotate oldest suitable food first.
Discard slimy, leaking, mouldy or strongly abnormal produce; trimming does not make every spoiled food safe.

source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/43 - Freeze garden produce safely.json

records.title: Freeze garden produce safely
records.summary: Prepare, package and freeze produce by a tested crop-specific method.
steps: Select sound produce at suitable maturity and follow a tested freezing guide for that exact crop.
Wash, trim and cut with clean tools; blanch vegetables when the tested method requires it.
Cool blanched food rapidly, drain well and package in freezer-rated containers with minimal excess air.
Label item, treatment and date; freeze promptly without overloading the freezer with warm packages.
Use quality changes, freezer damage and outage history to decide use; freezing does not restore spoiled food.

source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/44 - Blanch vegetables before freezing.json

records.title: Blanch vegetables before freezing
records.summary: Use the tested time and immediate cooling needed to protect frozen quality.
steps: Find the exact blanching method and time for the vegetable and cut size.
Bring the specified water or steam system to full operating condition before adding a measured batch.
Start timing only as directed after the process returns to the required condition.
Transfer immediately to abundant cold or ice water for the specified cooling period.
Drain thoroughly before packing; under-blanching and over-blanching both reduce quality.

source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/45 - Dry culinary herbs safely.json

records.title: Dry culinary herbs safely
records.summary: Dry correctly identified clean herbs rapidly enough to prevent mould.
steps: Harvest healthy correctly identified leaves before they are dirty, diseased or heavily damaged.
Follow a tested air-drying or dehydrator method appropriate to the herb and local humidity.
Spread thinly with good airflow and protect from dust, insects and direct contamination.
Continue until the tested endpoint is reached; cool before sealing so condensation does not form.
Store airtight, dark and labelled; discard any batch that develops moisture, mould or abnormal odour.

source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/46 - Dehydrate fruit and vegetables.json

records.title: Dehydrate fruit and vegetables
records.summary: Control preparation, temperature, dryness and conditioning for stable dried food.
steps: Use a current tested method for the exact fruit or vegetable, including any pretreatment.
Cut pieces uniformly and arrange in a single uncrowded layer.
Maintain the specified dehydrator temperature and airflow; sun drying is not safe or suitable for every food or climate.
Test the stated final texture after cooling, not while food is still warm.
Condition and package as the method directs; inspect jars for condensation and return inadequately dried food to the dehydrator promptly.

source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/47 - Refrigerator pickles versus shelf-stable pickles.json

records.title: Refrigerator pickles versus shelf-stable pickles
records.summary: Do not confuse a refrigerated acidified recipe with a processed shelf-stable product.
steps: Choose a current tested recipe and identify whether it is refrigerator-only or designed for canning.
Use the exact vinegar acidity, food amounts and jar size specified; do not dilute or alter proportions.
For refrigerator pickles, cool and keep continuously refrigerated for the stated period.
For shelf-stable pickles, use the complete heat-processing method and altitude adjustment in the tested recipe.
Discard jars with failed seals, leakage, spurting, mould or uncertain processing.

source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/48 - Controlled vegetable fermentation.json

records.title: Controlled vegetable fermentation
records.summary: Use tested salt, temperature, submersion and observation controls rather than improvising.
steps: Use a current tested recipe for the exact fermented product and batch size.
Measure ingredients, salt or brine exactly with clean equipment.
Keep vegetables submerged as the method specifies and use a clean suitable food-grade vessel.
Maintain the stated fermentation temperature and inspect regularly for the normal versus unsafe signs described by the recipe.
Refrigerate, process or store only as the tested method directs; discard soft, slimy, mouldy or foul-smelling failures.

source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/49 - Boiling-water canning for tested acid foods.json

records.title: Boiling-water canning for tested acid foods
records.subcategory: Boiling-water canning for tested acid foods
records.summary: Use boiling-water processing only for products covered by a current tested acid-food recipe.
steps: Confirm the recipe is current, tested and specifically intended for boiling-water canning.
Use the stated ingredient proportions, jar type, headspace and preparation; do not add extra low-acid vegetables.
Process for the full stated time, adjusting for altitude exactly as directed.
Cool undisturbed, verify the seal by the approved method and label the date.
Refrigerate and use promptly any jar that fails to seal only when the tested instructions permit; otherwise discard safely.

source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/50 - Pressure canning low-acid foods.json

records.title: Pressure canning low-acid foods
records.summary: Low-acid vegetables require a tested pressure-canning process, not boiling water alone.
steps: Use a current tested pressure-canning recipe for the exact food, jar size and preparation style.
Use a real pressure canner in working condition; inspect the seal, vent, gauge and manufacturer requirements.
Vent, pressurise, time and maintain pressure exactly as directed, including altitude adjustment.
Allow natural depressurisation and open only when the canner is safely at zero pressure.
If pressure drops below the required level, follow the tested reprocessing rule for the full process; never shorten the time.

source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/51 - Home-canning botulism warning signs.json

records.title: Home-canning botulism warning signs
records.summary: Reject unsafe jars without tasting; botulinum toxin may have no visible, smelled or tasted warning.
steps: Do not taste food from a jar with unknown recipe, process, pressure, time, seal or storage history.
Treat a leaking, bulging, cracked, spurting, foaming, mouldy or abnormally odorous jar as unsafe.
Keep people and animals away while following official disposal instructions that avoid splashing or skin contact.
If anyone develops possible botulism symptoms after preserved food, seek emergency medical help immediately and report the food history.
Prevent recurrence by using only current tested recipes and the correct canning equipment.

source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/52 - Collect rainwater for garden irrigation.json

records.title: Collect rainwater for garden irrigation
records.summary: Treat roof runoff as non-potable water; prefer verified safe water for edible crops and follow current local health guidance.
records.content: Use the steps as a conservative offline checklist, then follow current local rules, official alerts, product labels and competent agricultural or food-safety advice.
steps: Check local rules, roof materials, gutters and the previous use of every tank or barrel before collection.
Fit a secure cover and screened openings so children, animals, debris and mosquitoes cannot enter.
Divert the dirtiest initial roof runoff where practical and keep fuel, pesticide, lead-painted or chemically treated surfaces out of the collection path.
Prefer public-system or otherwise verified safe water for edible crops. If current local guidance permits collected rainwater, apply it at soil level and avoid splashing edible parts.
Inspect after storms for odour, algae, sediment, leaks and mosquito breeding; clean and isolate questionable water.
warnings: Rainwater is not automatically safe. CDC advises using public-system tap water or bottled water, when possible, for watering plants you plan to eat.
Never connect a rain barrel directly to drinking-water plumbing or allow backflow into it.
common_mistakes: Scaling up before a small controlled trial.

source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/53 - Greywater and wastewater safety boundaries.json

records.title: Greywater and wastewater safety boundaries
records.summary: Do not improvise wastewater irrigation for edible crops; it requires local rules and risk controls beyond ordinary garden practice.
steps: Identify the exact source: shower, laundry, kitchen, toilet, sewage, industrial or flood water are not interchangeable.
Check local public-health, plumbing and agricultural rules before designing any reuse system.
Keep untreated sewage, toilet waste, kitchen grease, chemical discharge and floodwater away from food-growing soil.
Where an approved greywater system exists, follow its treatment, subsurface delivery, crop restrictions, monitoring and maintenance requirements.
Switch to a safer water source whenever illness, odour, surfacing water, chemical contamination or system failure is suspected.
warnings: Boiling does not make chemically contaminated water suitable for irrigation or food handling.
Do not use this guide as a design standard for sewage or greywater systems.
common_mistakes: Scaling up before a small controlled trial.

source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/54 - Save seed first from suitable self-pollinating crops.json

records.title: Save seed first from suitable self-pollinating crops
records.subcategory: Save seed first from suitable self-pollinating crops
records.summary: Begin seed saving with healthy, correctly identified, open-pollinated plants whose seed behaviour is easier to manage.
steps: Confirm the crop and variety and whether it is open-pollinated, hybrid, treated, patented or subject to local seed rules.
Select several healthy, true-to-type plants rather than saving from one accidental survivor.
Keep plants intended for seed clearly labelled and allow seed to reach the crop-appropriate maturity.
Harvest in dry conditions where possible and keep each variety separate through cleaning.
Plant a small trial next season and compare health, uniformity and useful traits before relying on the lot.
warnings: Seed from hybrids may not reproduce the same crop traits in the next generation.
Do not save seed from diseased plants or lots with uncertain identity.
common_mistakes: Scaling up before a small controlled trial.

source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/55 - Dry, label and store home-saved seed.json

records.title: Dry, label and store home-saved seed
records.subcategory: Dry, label and store home-saved seed
records.summary: Protect viability by drying seed correctly, preventing moisture return and keeping complete lot records.
steps: Remove pulp, chaff and visibly damaged seed using the crop-appropriate dry or wet cleaning method.
Dry seed in a shaded, ventilated, protected place until it reaches the safe condition described for that crop.
Package only fully dried seed in clean labelled containers; include crop, variety, location, harvest year and any treatment.
Store cool, dark and dry, protected from insects, rodents and temperature swings.
Inspect periodically and run a labelled germination test before committing scarce bed space.
warnings: Sealing seed while still damp can cause mould, heating and rapid loss of viability.
Keep treated planting seed physically separate from food grain.
common_mistakes: Scaling up before a small controlled trial.

source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/56 - Support pollination and fruit set.json

records.title: Support pollination and fruit set
records.summary: Protect flowering access, identify pollination needs and avoid treating every failed flower as a fertilizer problem.
steps: Identify whether the crop is self-pollinating, wind-pollinated, insect-pollinated or requires another compatible variety.
Provide continuous suitable flowering habitat and clean shallow water nearby without creating mosquito breeding.
Avoid unnecessary broad-spectrum pesticide use, especially while crops or nearby plants are flowering.
For protected or indoor crops, use the crop-appropriate hand-pollination or vibration method only when needed.
Record temperature, wind, pollinator activity and fruit set before changing irrigation or fertilizer.
warnings: Do not introduce purchased insects or move wild pollinator nests without expert and legal guidance.
Pesticide labels and local pollinator-protection rules take priority over this summary.
common_mistakes: Scaling up before a small controlled trial.

source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/57 - Use a cold frame or cover for simple season extension.json

records.title: Use a cold frame or cover for simple season extension
records.subcategory: Use a cold frame or cover for simple season extension
records.summary: Extend mild-season production with ventilation, anchoring and daily temperature checks rather than sealed plastic heat traps.
steps: Choose a stable sunny location that drains safely and does not block exits or access.
Use food-growing-safe materials and anchor every cover against local wind.
Place a minimum–maximum thermometer at crop level and check it on sunny and cold days.
Vent before overheating, close before damaging cold and water only after checking soil moisture.
Remove or open covers when pollinator access is needed and inspect for trapped pests or disease.
warnings: A closed transparent cover can overheat rapidly even when outdoor air feels cool.
Do not use heaters, flames or improvised electrical equipment inside a small cover.
common_mistakes: Scaling up before a small controlled trial.

source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/58 - Build a safer balcony food garden.json

records.title: Build a safer balcony food garden
records.subcategory: Build a safer balcony food garden
records.summary: Control structural load, wind, drainage, falling objects and emergency access before adding containers.
steps: Obtain the building rules and professional load guidance when the safe capacity is not known.
Estimate the wet weight of containers, soil, stored water, shelving and people; spread loads only as professionally advised.
Secure pots, trellises and tools so wind cannot send them over an edge.
Collect or direct drainage without flooding neighbours, walls, outlets or walking surfaces.
Keep doors, fire routes, drains and maintenance access completely clear.
warnings: Wet growing media and stored water are much heavier than dry containers.
Do not drill, anchor or alter a balcony structure without authorization and competent guidance.
common_mistakes: Scaling up before a small controlled trial.

source_groups.path: Verified - Food Growing and Preservation/59 - Raw sprout food-safety boundaries.json

records.title: Raw sprout food-safety boundaries
records.summary: Sprouting seed in warm humid conditions can also support harmful bacteria; raw sprouts are not a risk-free emergency crop.
steps: Use seed sold for edible sprouting from a trustworthy source, not treated garden seed.
Sanitise hands, containers and work surfaces and use safe water throughout.
Keep batches separate, dated and small enough to inspect; discard any batch with abnormal odour, slime, mould or poor drainage.
Refrigerate finished sprouts promptly and prevent contact with raw meat, dirty produce or contaminated water.
For people at higher risk of foodborne illness, choose thoroughly cooked sprouts or another cooked crop instead of raw sprouts.
warnings: Rinsing cannot guarantee removal of pathogens that may be inside sprout tissue.
Never eat garden seed labelled as treated, coated or not for food use.
common_mistakes: Scaling up before a small controlled trial.

records.title: Triage a food garden during drought
records.subcategory: Triage a food garden during drought
records.summary: Protect drinking water first, then concentrate limited irrigation on the crops most likely to produce useful food.
steps: Follow official restrictions and reserve safe drinking, cooking and hygiene water before garden irrigation.
List crops by remaining time to harvest, food value, current health and water needed to finish.
Stop new sowing and remove failed or low-value plants that consume scarce water without realistic yield.
Mulch suitable soil, shade vulnerable containers, repair leaks and water the root zone slowly during the lower-evaporation part of the day.
Record water used and harvest gained so the next planting plan fits the reliable supply.
warnings: Do not divert water from essential human or animal needs to keep every plant alive.
Salty, sewage-contaminated, fuel-contaminated or chemically contaminated water can damage soil, crops and health.

records.title: Greece emergency call and 112 alert quick card
records.summary: Use 112 free of charge in Greece or elsewhere in the EU when immediate emergency assistance is required.
records.content: 112 connects urgent incidents with the appropriate emergency services. Call only for a real emergency. Give your exact location, what happened, current hazards, and how many people may need help. Follow the operator’s instructions and keep the line available.
steps: Move away from immediate danger if you can do so safely.
Call 112 and state the location first.
Describe the incident, hazards, number of people, and urgent symptoms.
Answer questions clearly and follow instructions.
Do not end the call until the operator says you may, unless remaining connected creates danger.
warnings: Do not make unnecessary calls to 112.
Do not enter fire, floodwater, unstable structures, traffic, or electrical hazards to obtain a better view.
common_mistakes: Giving a long story before the location.
Assuming the operator already knows the exact apartment, floor, rural road, beach, or trail position.
alternatives: If a voice call is impossible, use another available phone or ask a nearby person to contact 112 while you maintain safety.
failure_signs: The call drops, the location is uncertain, conditions worsen, or a new hazard blocks access.
when_not_to_use: Do not use 112 for routine information, non-urgent complaints, or test calls.
records.short_term: Keep the route clear for responders and assign someone to guide them from a safe point.
records.long_term: Store your address, building access details, medical needs, and emergency contacts offline and rehearse a concise emergency report.
records.if_method_fails: Move to a safer reception area if possible, retry, ask another person to call, and use any locally available emergency channel.
records.environment_notes: In remote, island, mountain, coastal, or construction locations, provide landmarks, access restrictions, gate codes, floor level, and visible hazards.
related_topics: Poisoning response and Greek Poison Centre

records.title: Household emergency plan and supply kit
records.summary: Prepare several days of water, food, medicines, light, communication, hygiene, documents, and a family contact plan.
records.content: A useful kit supports drinking, sanitation, essential medication, lighting, communication, and evacuation without depending on immediate shops or utilities. Ready.gov recommends one gallon of water per person per day for several days; this project rounds that to about 4 litres per person per day.
materials: about 4 litres of water per person per day for several days
non-perishable food and manual can opener
torch, batteries, radio, power banks and charging cables
copies of identification, contacts and key documents
steps: List household members, pets, medicines, mobility needs, and equipment that depends on power.
Choose meeting points and an out-of-area contact.
Pack supplies in portable containers and label dates.
Store additional supplies at home where heat, water, and pests will not damage them.
Review water, food, batteries, medicines, and documents on a fixed schedule.
warnings: Water needs increase with heat, heavy work, illness, pregnancy, breastfeeding, children, pets, and sanitation demands.
Do not store fuel, loose chemicals, or leaking batteries with food, water, or medicines.
common_mistakes: Buying equipment without practising with it.
Forgetting prescriptions, glasses, hearing-aid batteries, chargers, pet carriers, or accessibility equipment.
alternatives: Build the kit gradually, starting with water, medicines, light, communication, and documents.
failure_signs: Expired items, damaged containers, dead batteries, missing medicines, or a plan no household member can explain.
when_not_to_use: Do not delay an ordered evacuation to finish packing.
records.short_term: Create a minimum 72-hour kit and a written contact/meeting plan.
records.long_term: Expand supplies according to local hazards and rotate them before expiry.
records.if_method_fails: Take the highest-priority available items: medicines, phone, identification, water, weather protection, keys, and evacuation information.
records.environment_notes: Adapt for apartments, vehicles, ferries, islands, rural roads, heat, winter weather, construction work, pets, and power-dependent medical equipment.
related_topics: Greece emergency call and 112 alert quick card

records.title: Earthquake immediate actions
records.summary: Protect yourself from falling objects during shaking, then check for injuries, fire, leaks, structural damage, and official instructions.
records.content: During strong shaking, the immediate priority is protection from falling glass, furniture, masonry, and electrical hazards. After shaking stops, expect aftershocks and do not re-enter a visibly damaged structure until authorities or qualified professionals consider it safe.
steps: If indoors, stay inside, move away from windows and tall unsecured objects, drop low, cover your head and neck, and hold on to sturdy shelter if available.
If outdoors, move to an open area away from buildings, walls, signs, trees, and power lines.
When shaking stops, check yourself and others, put on shoes, and watch for debris.
If you smell gas, see fire, sparking, damaged wiring, or major structural damage, move away without operating switches or flames.
Use stairs rather than lifts and follow official instructions.
warnings: Aftershocks can cause additional collapse.
Do not enter damaged buildings or touch fallen electrical lines.
common_mistakes: Running through falling debris during shaking.
Standing in doorways without knowing whether they provide protection.
Using a lift after the earthquake.
alternatives: If no sturdy table is nearby, get low beside an interior wall away from glass and protect the head and neck.
failure_signs: Cracking or leaning walls, falling masonry, fire, gas odour, sparking, jammed doors, or repeated aftershocks.
when_not_to_use: Do not remain under visibly failing ceilings or beside fire, gas, chemical, or electrical hazards.
records.short_term: Account for people, treat immediate injuries within your training, and move to a safe assembly point if evacuation is necessary.
records.long_term: Secure furniture, identify utility shutoffs, store supplies, and practise household earthquake actions.
records.if_method_fails: Choose the nearest position that reduces exposure to falling objects and protect the head and neck until movement becomes safer.
records.environment_notes: On the coast, follow official tsunami instructions after strong or long shaking. In construction sites, avoid cranes, scaffolds, excavations, suspended loads, and partially completed structures.
related_topics: Household emergency plan and supply kit

records.title: Flood route and electrical safety
records.summary: Move away from underground and low areas, never cross moving water, avoid electrical hazards, and return only when authorities say it is safe.
records.content: Floodwater can hide missing road surfaces, open drains, contamination, current, and energized equipment. Greek Civil Protection advises moving to a secure higher point, not crossing torrents on foot or by car, and changing direction when a road is flooded.
steps: Follow warnings early and limit travel.
Leave basements, underground parking, stream beds, and other low areas.
Move to a secure higher point using a route that is not flooded.
Stop and change direction at flooded roads or crossings.
Stay away from wires, substations, damaged electrical equipment, and stagnant water near possible electrical faults.
Return only after official clearance and inspect utilities before use.
warnings: Do not walk or drive through moving water or torrents.
Floodwater may be contaminated and may conceal sharp objects, holes, and unstable ground.
common_mistakes: Assuming a familiar road or shallow-looking crossing is safe.
Entering a basement to save property after water begins rising.
alternatives: Use a preselected higher route or remain at a safe upper level while contacting emergency services if all exits are hazardous.
failure_signs: Rapidly rising water, moving debris, vehicle loss of traction, current around legs, sparking, sewage odour, or unstable ground.
when_not_to_use: Do not attempt property recovery, pumping, or electrical restoration while water is present or the structure is unassessed.
records.short_term: Reach a safe higher location, report trapped or missing people, and avoid contaminated water.
records.long_term: Map flood history, safe high points, blocked-drain risks, and routes that do not cross torrents.
records.if_method_fails: Stop movement, retreat to the last secure point, call 112, and make your location visible without entering the water.
records.environment_notes: Urban underpasses, basement garages, island roads, river crossings, and construction excavations can fill rapidly.
related_topics: Greece emergency call and 112 alert quick card

records.title: Wildfire warning and evacuation readiness
records.summary: Prevent ignition, report fire immediately, prepare the property before danger, and strictly follow official relocation instructions and routes.
records.content: Wildfire conditions can change faster than a household can react. Keep access clear, remove dry vegetation and flammable material according to local rules, prepare transport and essential supplies, and leave promptly when authorities order relocation.
steps: During high-risk periods, avoid outdoor burning, sparks, and open flames near dry vegetation.
If you see a fire, call 199 or 112 immediately and report the exact location, direction, and vegetation involved.
Keep gates and access routes available for emergency vehicles.
Prepare people, pets, medicines, documents, and transport before smoke or flame blocks routes.
If organised relocation is ordered, follow the authorities’ route and timing without delay.
warnings: Do not wait for visible flames before acting on an evacuation order.
Do not drive into dense smoke or use an unconfirmed route.
common_mistakes: Returning for property after evacuation begins.
Blocking access with vehicles or hoses.
Relying on a single exit route.
alternatives: If the planned route is blocked, use the official alternate route or contact 112 from the safest available shelter; do not improvise through fire or dense smoke.
failure_signs: Ash or embers, falling visibility, strong radiant heat, blocked roads, power loss, or official alerts naming your area.
when_not_to_use: Do not remain to defend property without training, suitable equipment, safe water supply, and a fully secure escape route.
records.short_term: Move early, account for everyone, and keep roads clear for emergency services.
records.long_term: Maintain defensible space and evacuation routes within applicable law and review the plan before each fire season.
records.if_method_fails: Use the safest substantial shelter available, close openings against smoke and embers where appropriate, call 112, and follow live official instructions.
records.environment_notes: Wind, slope, dry vegetation, narrow island or village roads, and smoke can remove escape options quickly.

records.title: Emergency drinking-water safety
records.summary: Use bottled or officially approved water first; boiling kills germs but does not remove chemicals, fuel, salt, or radioactive contamination.
records.content: When water safety is uncertain, follow the local advisory. For microbial contamination, CDC guidance says to bring clear water to a full rolling boil for 1 minute, or 3 minutes above about 2,000 metres, then cool it naturally and store it in a clean covered container. Boiling does not remove chemicals.
materials: clean cloth or coffee filter for cloudy water
steps: Check the official advisory and identify whether the problem is germs, chemicals, salt, fuel, or another contaminant.
Use bottled water when authorities recommend it.
For germ contamination only, let cloudy water settle or filter it through a clean cloth, then boil the clearer water.
Maintain a full rolling boil for 1 minute; above about 2,000 metres, boil for 3 minutes.
Cool without adding ice and store in a clean, sanitized, tightly covered container.
warnings: Boiling does not remove chemicals, petroleum, salt, heavy metals, or radioactive material.
Do not use floodwater or water with fuel, chemical, unusual colour, or unusual odour unless authorities specifically declare a safe treatment.
common_mistakes: Assuming a household filter makes advisory water safe without boiling.
Adding unsafe ice after boiling.
Touching the inside of clean lids or containers.
alternatives: Use sealed bottled water or an authority-approved treatment method appropriate to the identified contaminant.
failure_signs: Continuing official prohibition, chemical odour, oily film, illness, damaged well, sewage intrusion, or inability to maintain clean storage.
when_not_to_use: Do not apply boiling as the only treatment when chemical, fuel, saltwater, or radioactive contamination is suspected.
records.short_term: Protect a clearly marked supply for drinking, food preparation, medicine, infant feeding, toothbrushing, and pet needs.
records.long_term: Store and rotate emergency water and keep containers away from fuel, pesticides, heat, and sunlight.
records.if_method_fails: Stop using the source, isolate it, switch to bottled or officially supplied water, and seek public-health guidance.
records.environment_notes: Water needs rise during heat, physical work, illness, pregnancy, breastfeeding, and when sanitation systems fail.
related_topics: Household emergency plan and supply kit
Food safety during a power outage

records.title: Food safety during a power outage
records.summary: Keep appliance doors closed: an unopened refrigerator is generally safe for up to 4 hours, a full freezer for 48 hours, and a half-full freezer for 24 hours.
records.content: Time and temperature determine food safety; smell and appearance are not reliable tests. CDC guidance gives the 4-hour refrigerator, 48-hour full-freezer, and 24-hour half-full-freezer limits when doors remain closed.
materials: paper and pen for outage time
steps: Record when power was lost and keep refrigerator and freezer doors closed.
After 4 hours, move refrigerated perishables to a cooler at 4°C or below if a cold source is available.
Use an appliance thermometer to verify food temperature when possible.
Discard perishable refrigerated food that has been above 4°C for 2 hours or more, or 1 hour in very hot conditions, following official guidance.
When uncertain, discard the food rather than tasting it.
warnings: Never taste food to decide whether it is safe.
Discard food contaminated by floodwater, sewage, chemicals, damaged packaging, or unsafe temperatures.
common_mistakes: Opening doors repeatedly.
Relying on smell, taste, or appearance.
Refreezing thawed food without checking temperature and ice crystals.
alternatives: Use shelf-stable food that requires little or no water and heat.
failure_signs: Unknown outage duration, temperature above safe limits, leaking packages, swelling cans, unusual texture, or flood exposure.
when_not_to_use: Do not serve uncertain food to infants, pregnant people, older adults, immunocompromised people, or anyone else.
records.short_term: Prioritise safe foods, label discard decisions, and protect drinking water from cross-contamination.
records.long_term: Keep thermometers in appliances, freeze water containers to add thermal mass, and plan shelf-stable meals.
records.if_method_fails: Discard uncertain perishables and switch to sealed shelf-stable food and safe water.
records.environment_notes: Outage times shorten when doors are opened, appliances start warm, or the surrounding temperature is high.
related_topics: Household emergency plan and supply kit

records.title: Generator and carbon monoxide safety
records.summary: Run fuel-burning generators only outdoors, more than 20 feet (about 6 metres) from windows, doors, and vents, with exhaust directed away.
records.content: Carbon monoxide is colourless and odourless. CDC guidance says never use a generator inside a home or garage, even with doors or windows open, and to place it outdoors more than 20 feet from openings.
materials: dry weather protection that preserves ventilation
steps: Place the generator outdoors, more than about 6 metres from windows, doors, and vents.
Point exhaust away from buildings and occupied areas.
Keep it dry without enclosing it or blocking airflow.
Use the manufacturer’s connection method; never back-feed a building through a wall outlet.
Install and test CO alarms near sleeping areas and on occupied levels.
Shut down and cool the generator before refuelling.
warnings: Never operate a generator in a house, garage, basement, shed, balcony enclosure, stairwell, or near open windows.
Headache, dizziness, weakness, nausea, chest pain, confusion, or collapse may indicate carbon monoxide poisoning; move to fresh air and call 112.
common_mistakes: Assuming an open garage door provides enough ventilation.
Placing the generator close to a neighbour’s window or shared air intake.
Refuelling while hot.
alternatives: Use charged power banks, battery lighting, or professionally installed backup systems for essential low-power needs.
failure_signs: CO alarm activation, exhaust entering a building, unstable operation, fuel leak, damaged cable, overheating, or symptoms in any person.
when_not_to_use: Do not use the generator when safe outdoor clearance, dry operation, correct cabling, or competent supervision cannot be maintained.
records.short_term: Stop the engine, move everyone to fresh air, and call 112 if exposure is suspected.
records.long_term: Arrange qualified electrical installation, maintain the generator, rotate fuel legally and safely, and test CO alarms monthly.
records.if_method_fails: Disconnect the load and stop using the generator; switch to non-combustion backup power or evacuate to a powered safe location.
records.environment_notes: Shared apartment courtyards, balconies, tents, caravans, construction cabins, and partially enclosed spaces can accumulate exhaust.

records.title: Heat illness recognition and escalation
records.summary: Confusion, altered speech, loss of consciousness, seizures, or very high body temperature suggest heat stroke and require immediate emergency care.
records.content: Heat stroke can cause permanent disability or death. Call 112, move the person to shade or a cool area, remove excess outer clothing, and cool rapidly while emergency help is coming. Do not give fluids to a person who is confused, unconscious, seizing, or unable to swallow safely.
steps: Stop work or exercise and move the person out of heat.
Call 112 immediately for confusion, altered speech, collapse, seizure, or suspected heat stroke.
Remove excess outer clothing and start rapid cooling with cool water, wet cloths, airflow, or a cold-water/ice bath when safely available.
Stay with the person and monitor breathing and responsiveness.
For milder heat exhaustion in an alert person, cool them and offer frequent small sips of cool water while arranging medical evaluation if symptoms are severe or do not improve.
warnings: Do not leave a confused or unconscious person alone.
Do not force fluids into anyone who cannot swallow safely.
Do not stop or change regular medication without medical advice.
common_mistakes: Waiting for sweating to stop before treating heat stroke.
Sending the person back to work after brief improvement.
Using alcohol or very sugary drinks for rehydration.
alternatives: Move to an air-conditioned public or private location and use available cool water and wet cloths while waiting for help.
failure_signs: Worsening confusion, collapse, seizure, breathing difficulty, chest pain, inability to drink, or no improvement with cooling.
when_not_to_use: Do not treat suspected heat stroke as simple dehydration or delay emergency care to measure temperature.
records.short_term: Continue cooling and monitoring until emergency services take over.
records.long_term: Plan work/rest cycles, acclimatisation, shade, water access, buddy checks, and medication review for heat exposure.
records.if_method_fails: Escalate immediately to 112 and use the fastest safe cooling method available while maintaining airway safety.
records.environment_notes: Risk rises with construction work, protective clothing, humidity, direct sun, poor airflow, chronic illness, some medicines, and lack of acclimatisation.

records.title: Poisoning response and Greek Poison Centre
records.summary: For severe symptoms or immediate danger call 112; Greece’s Poison Centre provides free 24/7 information at 210 7793777.
records.content: The Greek Ministry of Health states that the national Poison Centre operates 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, and provides information free of charge at 210 7793777. Keep the product container, label, medicine package, or a photo available, but do not delay emergency action.
materials: fresh air or clean-water access only when safe
steps: Move away from an active chemical, smoke, or gas hazard without exposing yourself.
Call 112 for breathing difficulty, collapse, seizure, severe confusion, chest pain, major burns, or immediate danger.

Prefer flashlights over candles. Keep exits clear. Put heat and cooking tasks on a schedule so tired people are not improvising at night. If anyone develops headache, dizziness, nausea, confusion, weakness, or unusual sleepiness near a burning device, move to fresh air and seek emergency help.

records.title: Wildfire-smoke health red flags
records.summary: Recognise when smoke exposure requires urgent movement to cleaner air and professional help, especially for vulnerable people.
records.content: Working sequence: Escalate for severe breathing difficulty, chest symptoms, confusion, fainting, blue or grey colour, inability to speak normally, or rapidly worsening established disease. Make the scene safe, use consent where possible, and call emergency services for immediate threats for “Wildfire-smoke health red flags”. Observe breathing, alertness, major bleeding, severe pain, temperature exposure, and rapid change without inventing a diagnosis for “Wildfire-smoke health red flags”. Give only low-risk care within training and follow the person’s established professional plan for medicines or chronic needs for “Wildfire-smoke health red flags”. Record time, observations, actions, medicines already taken, allergies, response, and who was contacted for “Wildfire-smoke health red flags”. Reassess frequently and arrange qualified help early when danger signs, uncertainty, or deterioration are present for “Wildfire-smoke health red flags”. Do not diagnose, prescribe, improvise dosing, perform invasive procedures, or delay emergency help in “Wildfire-smoke health red flags”. Protect privacy and infection-control boundaries, but never let paperwork delay lifesaving action in “Wildfire-smoke health red flags”.

Confirm the reason for movement, official instruction, destination, primary route, fallback route, weather, daylight, and transport limits for “Wildfire early-departure trigger”. Mark hazards such as fire, smoke, floodwater, damaged bridges, unstable slopes, crowds, poor visibility, and restricted areas for “Wildfire early-departure trigger”. Match pace, load, rest, assistance, and transport to children, older adults, disability, illness, animals, and the slowest safe member for “Wildfire early-departure trigger”. Leave a departure time, route, destination, group list, check-in schedule, and missed-contact rule with a trusted person for “Wildfire early-departure trigger”. Stop at planned checkpoints, compare real conditions with the map, and turn back or divert before the route becomes trapping or irreversible for “Wildfire early-departure trigger”. Never enter moving floodwater, wildfire closure, smoke-obscured road, unstable slope, damaged structure, or officially restricted route in “Wildfire early-departure trigger”. Do not split the group without a written destination, communication rule, responsible adults, and reunification plan in “Wildfire early-departure trigger”.

Επίλεξε κύρια διαδρομή, εναλλακτική διαδρομή και προστατευμένο σημείο αναμονής γνωστό στους διασώστες. Γράψε πώς μετακινείται, διπλώνει ή τροφοδοτείται η συσκευή, πώς αποφεύγεται ζημιά και ποιες ενέργειες απαιτούν εκπαιδευμένους διασώστες. Εξάσκησε επικοινωνία και μετακίνηση χωρίς τεχνικές ανύψωσης ή μεταφοράς στις οποίες οι βοηθοί δεν έχουν εκπαιδευτεί. Όριο ασφάλειας: Μην χρησιμοποιείς ανελκυστήρα σε φωτιά ή όταν οι αρχές τον θεωρούν μη ασφαλή. Μην χωρίζεις άτομο από απαραίτητο βοήθημα εκτός αν το απαιτεί η άμεση ασφάλεια ζωής.

records.content: Ακολουθία ενεργειών: Γράψε προτιμώμενη γλώσσα, τρόπο επικοινωνίας, επαφές ανάγκης, φάρμακα, αλλεργίες και αν απαιτείται διερμηνέας. Ενεργοποίησε δόνηση, φωτεινή ειδοποίηση και ρυθμίσεις έκτακτης ανάγκης και δοκίμασέ τες με άλλο άτομο. Ετοίμασε σύντομες φράσεις για ΒΟΗΘΕΙΑ, ΦΩΤΙΑ, ΙΑΤΡΙΚΟ, ΠΑΓΙΔΕΥΜΕΝΟΣ, ΑΣΦΑΛΗΣ, ΤΟΠΟΘΕΣΙΑ και ΧΡΕΙΑΖΟΜΑΙ ΔΙΕΡΜΗΝΕΑ στα ελληνικά και αγγλικά. Δείξε την κάρτα νωρίς στους διασώστες και επιβεβαίωσε τις οδηγίες γραπτώς ή με επανάληψη. Όριο ασφάλειας: Μην υποθέτεις ότι σειρήνα, προφορική οδηγία ή τηλεφωνική κλήση έγινε αντιληπτή. Μην αφαιρείς ακουστικό εξοπλισμό χωρίς οδηγία του ατόμου εκτός αν το απαιτεί άμεσος κίνδυνος.
steps: Γράψε προτιμώμενη γλώσσα, τρόπο επικοινωνίας, επαφές ανάγκης, φάρμακα, αλλεργίες και αν απαιτείται διερμηνέας.
warnings: Μην υποθέτεις ότι σειρήνα, προφορική οδηγία ή τηλεφωνική κλήση έγινε αντιληπτή.

records.summary: Διατήρησε διαδρομές, σημάνσεις, αντικείμενα και προφορική καθοδήγηση προβλέψιμα ώστε ξαφνική ακαταστασία ή μετακίνηση να μην δημιουργήσει δεύτερο κίνδυνο.
records.content: Ακολουθία ενεργειών: Κράτησε την κανονική διαδρομή προς τις εξόδους ελεύθερη και μην μετακινείς έπιπλα χωρίς ενημέρωση. Χρησιμοποίησε ανάγλυφες ή υψηλής αντίθεσης σημάνσεις για τσάντα ανάγκης, φάρμακα, νερό, κλειδιά και χειριστήρια παροχών. Κατά την καθοδήγηση πρόσφερε αγκώνα, περιέγραψε σκαλοπάτια και εμπόδια πριν φτάσετε σε αυτά και άφησε το άτομο να ορίζει τον ρυθμό. Δημιούργησε εναλλακτική διαδρομή και εξάσκησέ την με το συνηθισμένο βοήθημα και σκύλο υπηρεσίας όπου ισχύει. Όριο ασφάλειας: Μην τραβάς, σπρώχνεις ή πιάνεις το άτομο ή το μπαστούνι του χωρίς προειδοποίηση. Μην χωρίζεις σκύλο υπηρεσίας από τον χειριστή του εκτός από άμεσο ανεξέλεγκτο κίνδυνο.

records.summary: Μείωσε την υπερφόρτωση με σύντομη οπτική ακολουθία, οικεία αντικείμενα, έναν υπεύθυνο επικοινωνίας και προβλέψιμες επιλογές.
records.content: Ακολουθία ενεργειών: Δημιούργησε ακολουθία πέντε βημάτων: παπούτσια, τσάντα, έξοδος, σημείο συνάντησης, επαφή. Αναγνώρισε ερεθίσματα, τρόπους ηρεμίας, κίνδυνο απομάκρυνσης, τρόπο επικοινωνίας και βασικές ρουτίνες. Χρησιμοποίησε έναν ήρεμο ομιλητή, σύντομες συγκεκριμένες φράσεις, επιπλέον χρόνο επεξεργασίας και δύο ασφαλείς επιλογές αντί για πολλές ερωτήσεις. Τοποθέτησε στοιχεία ταυτοποίησης και υποστήριξης μέσα στα ρούχα ή στην τσάντα ανάγκης λαμβάνοντας υπόψη την ιδιωτικότητα. Όριο ασφάλειας: Μην συγκρατείς, απειλείς ή τιμωρείς συμπεριφορά δυσφορίας εκτός αν εκπαιδευμένοι διασώστες πρέπει να αποτρέψουν άμεση βλάβη. Μην αφαιρείς απαραίτητα αντικείμενα επικοινωνίας ή ηρεμίας μόνο για να ελαφρύνει η τσάντα.

records.title: Εφεδρικό σχέδιο για ιατρικές συσκευές που εξαρτώνται από ρεύμα
records.summary: Κατέγραψε κατανάλωση, διάρκεια μπαταρίας, ασφαλή φόρτιση, κλινικές επαφές και κριτήρια μετακίνησης πριν από διακοπή ρεύματος.
records.content: Ακολουθία ενεργειών: Κατέγραψε τάση, κατανάλωση, διάρκεια μπαταρίας, συναγερμούς, αναλώσιμα και αν η διακοπή είναι άμεσα επικίνδυνη. Δοκίμασε κάθε εγκεκριμένη εφεδρική πηγή υπό καθοδήγηση προμηθευτή ή κλινικής ομάδας και σήμανε τα βήματα σύνδεσης. Όρισε όριο μπαταρίας και διάρκεια διακοπής που ενεργοποιεί επικοινωνία με 112, κλινικό, προμηθευτή ή ασφαλή χώρο με ρεύμα. Κράτησε μαζί και έτοιμα για μετακίνηση τη συσκευή, τους σωλήνες, τις μπαταρίες, τα έγγραφα και το βοήθημα μεταφοράς. Όριο ασφάλειας: Μην συνδέεις ιατρική συσκευή σε αυτοσχέδια ή ασύμβατη πηγή ενέργειας. Μην περιμένεις τον τελευταίο συναγερμό μπαταρίας πριν οργανώσεις ειδικευμένη βοήθεια ή μετακίνηση.
steps: Κατέγραψε τάση, κατανάλωση, διάρκεια μπαταρίας, συναγερμούς, αναλώσιμα και αν η διακοπή είναι άμεσα επικίνδυνη.
warnings: Μην συνδέεις ιατρική συσκευή σε αυτοσχέδια ή ασύμβατη πηγή ενέργειας.

records.title: Πακέτο επανένωσης παιδιού
records.summary: Προετοίμασε επαληθευμένη ταυτότητα, εξουσιοδοτημένες επαφές, σημεία συνάντησης, ιατρικές ανάγκες και κανόνες παράδοσης πριν συμβεί χωρισμός.
records.content: Πρακτική ακολουθία: Χρησιμοποίησε πρόσφατες φωτογραφίες, ονόματα, έμπιστες επαφές, στοιχεία σχολείου ή φροντίδας, αλλεργίες, ανάγκες επικοινωνίας, δύο σημεία συνάντησης και κανόνα μη παράδοσης σε ανεπιβεβαίωτο άτομο. Όρισε την ακριβή απόφαση, τον υπεύθυνο, την προθεσμία και τον επόμενο έλεγχο για το θέμα «Πακέτο επανένωσης παιδιού». Χώρισε τα επιβεβαιωμένα γεγονότα από υποθέσεις, αιτήματα και ανεπιβεβαίωτες αναφορές για το θέμα «Πακέτο επανένωσης παιδιού». Κατέγραψε πόρους που δόθηκαν, επηρεαζόμενα άτομα, όρια συναίνεσης και άλυτους κινδύνους για το θέμα «Πακέτο επανένωσης παιδιού». Χρησιμοποίησε δεύτερο ελεγκτή για σημαντικά σύνολα, ονόματα, διαδρομές ή αποφάσεις ασφάλειας για το θέμα «Πακέτο επανένωσης παιδιού». Κλείσε τον κύκλο με χρονολογημένη παράδοση και μία σαφώς ανατεθειμένη επόμενη ενέργεια για το θέμα «Πακέτο επανένωσης παιδιού». Μην εκθέτεις ιδιωτικά στοιχεία ταυτότητας, υγείας, τοποθεσίας ή επαφών πέρα από την πραγματική ανάγκη στο θέμα «Πακέτο επανένωσης παιδιού». Η πίεση χρόνου δεν δικαιολογεί εξαναγκασμό, διάκριση, κλοπή, ταπείνωση ή κρυφές αποφάσεις στο θέμα «Πακέτο επανένωσης παιδιού».

Συνέχισε με το εξής: Όρισε την ακριβή απόφαση, τον υπεύθυνο, την προθεσμία και τον επόμενο έλεγχο για το θέμα «Πακέτο επανένωσης παιδιού». Πριν επαναλάβεις τη διαδικασία, επιβεβαίωσε ότι απουσιάζει αυτό το σημάδι αποτυχίας: Σταμάτησε και επανεκτίμησε το θέμα «Πακέτο επανένωσης παιδιού» όταν η ευθύνη γίνεται ασαφής και η ίδια εργασία επαναλαμβάνεται ή ξεχνιέται.

records.title: Σάκος και σχέδιο έγκαιρης επικοινωνίας για διακοπή αιμοκάθαρσης
records.summary: Εξατομικευμένη κάρτα συνέχειας για κλείσιμο μονάδας, αποτυχία μεταφοράς, εκκένωση, αρχεία, φάρμακα, οδηγίες διατροφής και υγρών και συμπτώματα επείγουσας φροντίδας.
materials: οδηγίες έκτακτης διατροφής και υγρών εγκεκριμένες από επαγγελματία υγείας
steps: Ζήτησε εκ των προτέρων γραπτό σχέδιο καταστροφής, εναλλακτικά κέντρα, μεταφορά, κανόνες φροντίδας αγγειακής πρόσβασης και προσωπικά όρια συμπτωμάτων.
Όταν υπάρχει πιθανότητα διακοπής, επικοινώνησε νωρίς με τη μονάδα, επιβεβαίωσε την επόμενη θεραπεία και μην πας σε εναλλακτικό κέντρο χωρίς αποδοχή.
Μετέφερε αρχεία θεραπείας, ταυτότητα, φάρμακα στην αρχική συσκευασία, στοιχεία πρόσβασης, αλλεργίες, πρόσφατες εξετάσεις αν έχουν δοθεί και εγκεκριμένες οδηγίες έκτακτης ανάγκης.
Ζήτησε επείγουσα βοήθεια για σοβαρή δύσπνοια, πόνο στο στήθος, σύγχυση, λιποθυμία, μεγάλη διόγκωση, ανεξέλεγκτη αιμορραγία ή λοίμωξη ή αστοχία πρόσβασης.
warnings: Μην αυτοσχεδιάζεις αλλαγές σε υγρά, αλάτι, κάλιο, φάρμακα ή θεραπεία.
Προστάτεψε την πρόσβαση αιμοκάθαρσης και μην επιτρέψεις χρήση από μη εκπαιδευμένο άτομο.
